block.txt: This Part applies to all private water trusts under Part 3 of the former Water Act 1912 that were in existence immediately before the repeal of that Part, but does not authorise the establishment of any new private water trusts.
In this Part—
member’s water entitlement means the part of the share component of an access licence held by or on behalf a private water trust that is available to a member.
private water trust means a trust constituted under Part 3 of the former Water Act 1912.
rules means the rules of a private water trust, as in force from time to time.
trust work means a water management work, or a proposed water management work, specified in the works plan for a private water trust.
trustee of a private water trust means a trustee elected under section 223.
works plan means the works plan for a private water trust specified for the trust, as in force from time to time.

heading.b: Requirements for access licences and approvals

block.txt: Nothing in this Part authorises a private water trust, the trustees of a trust or landholder to do anything for which this Act requires an access licence or approval unless the private water trust, trustees on behalf of the trust or landholder holds an appropriate access licence or approval.

content.txt: ch 4, pt 4, div 2: Subst 2010 No 133, Sch 2[59].

block.txt: The number of trustees of a private water trust is to be the number when section 220 commenced.
The trustees of a trust are to be elected.
The trustees must elect one of the trustees as chairperson of the trust.
The trustees have the following functions—
to direct, control and manage the affairs of the trust, in accordance with this Act, the regulations and the rules,
any other functions conferred on the trustees by or under this Act.
The trustees are to act for and on behalf of the trust.
A trustee holds office for the term prescribed by the rules.
The regulations may prescribe the circumstances in which a trustee ceases to be a trustee.
For the purposes of this Act and the regulations, a trust is taken to be the holder of any access licence or approval that is held by any former or other current trustees on behalf of the trust.

A trustee must, as soon as practicable after ceasing to be a trustee, take all necessary action to transfer any interest in property held by the former trustee on behalf of the trust to the trustees of the trust or the trust.

heading.b: Water supply and other functions of trusts

block.txt: A private water trust has the following functions—
to provide, maintain or operate a water supply system, water distribution system or drainage system,
any other function conferred or imposed on the trust by or under this or any other Act.
The trust may supply water—
under an access licence or approval held by the trustees or trust, or
for the purpose of an access licence or approval held by a member whose member’s water entitlement has been transformed under Division 4.
A private water trust may, from time to time, amend or replace the rules of the trust.
The rules may make provision for or with respect to the following matters—
elections of trustees,
the trustees and procedures of the trustees,
the members of the trust,
meetings of the trust,
meetings of trustees of the trust,
the voting rights of members of the trust, or classes of members of the trust,
new members of the trust,
the functions of the trust that may be exercised only by resolution at a meeting of the members of the trust,
the imposition of rates and charges on members of the trust for services (including water) provided by the trust,
the regulation of a water supply, water distribution or drainage system provided by the trust,
the regulation of the supply, taking or use of water provided by a water supply or water distribution system provided by the trust,
the regulation of the draining or disposal of water through a drainage system provided by the trust,
the financial management and systems of the trust,
the manner in which the rules are to be amended or replaced,
any other matters prescribed by the regulations,
any other matters necessary for, or ancillary to, the purposes of the trust.
The rules must—
not be inconsistent with this Act or the regulations, and
comply with any requirements prescribed by the regulations.
A trust must notify changes to the rules, or replaced rules, in the manner prescribed by the regulations.

The rules are binding on the trustees and members of the trust and landholders to whom the trust provides services and it is presumed that the trustees, members and landholders have notice of the rules.
A rule has no effect to the extent to which it is inconsistent with this Act or the regulations.

A trust must not make a change to a rule unless the proposed change has been approved by at least two thirds of the members of the trust who are entitled to vote on the question or the change is authorised by the rules.
The regulations may vary the proportion of members of a trust who must approve any such change or any class of change.

heading.b: Trustees must provide copy of rules

block.txt: A trustee of a private water trust must, if required to do so by the Minister, provide the Minister with a copy of the rules of the trust.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

A private water trust must, on the request of a member of the trust and payment by the member of the fee (if any) prescribed by the rules of the trust, provide the member with a copy of the rules of the trust.
A private water trust or the trustees of a trust may by instrument in writing delegate—
to any trustee or to any member of the trust, or
to any employee of the trust,
any of their functions, other than this power of delegation.

content.txt: ch 4, pt 4, div 3: Subst 2010 No 133, Sch 2[59].

block.txt: A private water trust may exercise the following functions for the purpose of its water supply, water distribution and drainage functions—
construct, install, maintain, operate and manage trust works,
repair, replace, maintain, remove, extend, connect, disconnect, improve or do any other things in relation to trust works that are necessary for the purpose of carrying out their functions.
A private water trust may enter into an arrangement with a landholder to provide services in relation to works that are not trust works.

heading.b: Members may be required to provide distribution works

block.txt: A private water trust may require a member of the trust, or a landholder who is supplied with water by the trust, to do any of the following—
to provide water delivery systems on a landholding to enable the supply of water to the land at the rate specified by the trust,
to provide water storage works in the locations, and of a kind, specified by the trust for water supplied for stock or domestic purposes,
to maintain any water delivery systems or water storage works on the land so as to enable the trust to properly exercise functions in relation to the supply of water.
The requirement is to be made by notice in writing given by the trust to the member or landholder.
A requirement may be made under this section only if it is necessary for the efficient or effective operation of trust works or the carrying out of the trust’s functions.

heading.b: Discontinuation of water supply by trust

block.txt: A private water trust may at any time suspend or restrict the supply of, or refuse to supply, water to a member or landholder if the trust is reasonably satisfied that any of the following circumstances exist—
the water that is available to the trust cannot meet the demand,
the water that is available to the trust is not suitable for the required purpose,
the trust is unable to provide sufficient conveyance water in connection with the operation of an irrigation system,
the trust is not lawfully able to supply the quantity of water,
the member or landholder has failed to pay charges or fees for water or other services provided by the trust,
the member or landholder has contravened or failed to comply with a condition on which water or drainage services are supplied by the trust,

the member or landholder has contravened or failed to comply with a requirement of the trust relating to the provision, maintenance or repair of distribution works or any other requirement made by the trust in accordance with this Act, the regulations or the rules,
the member or landholder has contravened or failed to comply with a requirement of this Act, the regulations or the rules,
the trust is unable to dispose of water draining into its drainage system because of the degraded quality of the water.
A private water trust that takes action under this section may reduce the amount of water available by different amounts or proportions according to such factors as it thinks fit.

heading.b: Supply of services to other persons

block.txt: A private water trust may enter into an agreement with a person who is not a member of the trust to supply water for the purpose of irrigating land or other purposes, or to drain water from land, by means of a water supply, water distribution or drainage system provided and managed by the trust.
A private water trust must not supply water for domestic purposes if a supply of water is available to the person from a local water utility or a major utility.
A private water trust may, by its employees or agents, enter onto land on which trust works are situated, or any other land, for the following purposes—
to carry out any of the trust’s functions in relation to trust works,
to read a meter that measures water supplied by the trust or monitors drainage for quantity or quality or both,

to carry out investigations or inspections, take levels, drill test bore-holes, dig trenches, make surveys and marks, and fix pegs and stakes, for the purposes of designing, constructing or determining the site of a proposed trust work,
to remove samples of materials from the land for the purpose of carrying out trust functions, but only if the landholder has been consulted and the views of the landholder have been considered,
to exercise any other powers that are incidental to the trust’s functions that are reasonably necessary for carrying out those functions.
The powers of entry conferred by this section are not to be exercised for a purpose referred to in subsection (1) (a), (c) or (d) without prior notice to the landholder of the land.
The trust must ensure that as little damage as possible is caused by the exercise of powers under this section and must repair any damage caused or pay compensation for the damage.
A works plan for a trust must—
identify the water management works or proposed works that are the trust works, and
specify the location of, and describe, the works, and
specify the land to which the works plan applies.
A works plan must comply with any requirements prescribed by the regulations and the rules.
A works plan may be amended or replaced if the amendment or replacement is consented to by any landholder on whose land affected works are situated or is authorised by the rules.
A works plan may specify works on land of former members of the trust who have transformed their member’s water entitlements.
Regulations may be made for or with respect to the keeping of, and provision of, copies of works plans.

heading.b: Sale and transformation of water entitlements

content.txt: ch 4, pt 4, div 4: Subst 2010 No 133, Sch 2[59].

block.txt: A private water trust may, if requested to do so by a member of the trust, determine the member’s water entitlement.
The trust must determine a member’s water entitlement if the request is made by a member who is supplied by the trust with water for irrigation.
The trust must have regard to the following matters when determining the member’s water entitlement—
the nature of agricultural activities on the land to which water is supplied,
the amount of water currently supplied to the member,
any present or past water sharing arrangements applicable to the member,
any other matter it considers relevant,
any other matter prescribed by the regulations.
A determination may specify the different parts of the member’s water entitlement that are available to the landholding for different purposes.
A determination must be in writing and comply with the requirements of the regulations. Notice of a determination must be given in writing by the trust to the member.
A determination may be varied or redetermined only on a further application made by the member within 3 months of the determination or in the circumstances prescribed by the regulations.

A person must not participate in a determination of a member’s water entitlement if the person or a member of the person’s immediate family (within the meaning of the regulations) has an interest in the entitlement.

heading.b: Sale or transfer of group entitlement

block.txt: A private water trust must not enter into a dealing to sell or mortgage the whole or part of the water entitlement of a trust under an access licence unless the dealing is permitted under, and is in accordance with, the rules of the trust.

heading.b: Sale or transfer of members’ water entitlements

block.txt: A member of a private water trust may sell or transfer the whole or any part of the member’s water entitlement to another member or to the trust.

A member must not sell or transfer the whole or part of the member’s water entitlement under this section unless the sale or transfer has been approved by the trust in accordance with the rules or the regulations.
A sale or transfer by a member does not affect the member’s membership of the trust, except as provided by this Act and the rules of the trust.

A private water trust may make an application under Division 4 of Part 2 of Chapter 3 for the purpose of wholly or partly transforming a member’s water entitlement into an access licence under this Act.
On transformation of the whole or part of a member’s water entitlement to an access licence—

the member is not entitled to vote (as a trustee) or as a member on any matter relating to the transformation of one or more other members’ water entitlements or the supply of water to members who have not transformed their water entitlements, and

the trust may continue to exercise functions in relation to any trust works that are located on the landholding (whether or not the trust is to deliver the member’s water entitlement under the access licence or the landholder remains a member of the trust).
If the whole of a person’s water entitlement is transformed and the person does not have a right to the delivery of that water by the trust—
the person ceases to be a member of the trust, and
the trust must not fix rates and charges in respect of the person’s landholding for that water (other than termination charges).
The rules may make provision for or with respect to other circumstances in which a person whose member’s water entitlement has been transformed ceases to be a member of the trust.
The trust may require a member to provide security as a condition of consent to transformation of the whole or part of the member’s water entitlement, subject to the regulations.
Without limiting subsection (5), the following kinds of security may be required by the trust—
a charge over a part of an irrigation right that is not transformed,
a charge over an access licence or other entitlement to water acquired by the person and resulting from the transformation,
a guarantee by an authorised deposit-taking institution,
a deposit lodged with the trust.

content.txt: ch 4, pt 4, div 5A: Ins 2010 No 133, Sch 1 [5]. Rep 2010 No 133, Sch 2[59].
ch 4, pt 4, div 5: Subst 2010 No 133, Sch 2[59].

heading.b: Changes in membership requiring works plan changes

block.txt: A private water trust must not make a change in membership that results in a consequential change to the works plan of the trust unless the proposed change to the works plan has been approved by at least two thirds of the members of the trust who are entitled to vote on the question.
The regulations may vary the proportion of the members of the trust who must approve any such change.
Any change to the works plan takes effect from the date approval is given or such other date (being an earlier or later date) as is specified in the approval.

heading.b: Application for amalgamation of private water trusts

block.txt: Two or more private water trusts may apply to the Minister to constitute one private water trust.
An application is—
to be in the approved form, and
to be accompanied by a works plan and proposed rules for the new trust, and
to be accompanied by any other information required by the Minister or prescribed by the regulations, and
to be accompanied by the fee (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
The Minister may grant an application to amalgamate 2 or more trusts if—
the Minister is satisfied that the purpose of the amalgamated trust is to provide, maintain or operate any or all of a water supply system, water distribution system or drainage system, and
the trust and any proposed works plan or rules of the trust comply with any requirements of this Act and the regulations.
The amalgamated private water trust is to be constituted by the Minister by order published on the NSW legislation website.
In addition to constituting the trust, the order must specify the following—
the name of the trust,
the water supply, water distribution or water drainage purposes of the trust,
the landholdings for which the trust may exercise functions and the works plan of the trust,
the members of the trust,
the trustees of the trust, pending the first election of trustees,
the date, time and place for the first election of the trustees,
the rules of the trust.
On the order being published or on such later day as may be specified in the order—
the new trust is constituted, and
the members of the trust are the members specified in the order, and
the rules and works plan specified by the order take effect, and
the amalgamated trusts are abolished, and
the new trust is taken for all purposes to be a continuation of and the same legal entity as each of the amalgamated trusts.
The new trust is not a NSW government agency.
If a member of a private water trust sells to a person land to which the trust provides or is able to provide water supply or drainage services—
the member ceases to be a member in respect of that land when that sale takes effect, and
the purchaser is taken to be a member of the trust when the sale takes effect, and
the purchaser has all the entitlements and liabilities of the vendor as a member, in respect of the land, that the vendor had immediately before the sale took effect.
A member of a trust who sells land as referred to in this section must notify the trust of the sale in accordance with any requirements of the regulations or the rules.
The subdivision of land by a member of a private water trust—
does not of itself entitle any other person to be a member of the trust or entitle any other person to be supplied with water or provided with drainage or other services by the trustees or trust, and
does not of itself affect any existing entitlement of any other person in relation to any such service, and
does not of itself affect any functions of the trustees or trust in relation to trust works.

heading.b: Conversion of private water trust to private water corporation

block.txt: A private water trust may apply to the Minister to convert the trust to a private water corporation.
An application is—
to be in the approved form, and
to be accompanied by a works plan for the corporation and proposed rules for the corporation, and
to be accompanied by any other information required by the Minister or prescribed by the regulations, and
to be accompanied by the fee (if any) prescribed by the regulations.
The Minister must not grant the application unless the Minister is satisfied that not less than two thirds of the members of the trust have approved of the application being made.
The application is to be dealt with as if it were an application for the constitution of a corporation made in accordance with Part 2.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the following matters—
the modification of the application of the provisions of Part 2 for the purposes of this section,
provisions of a savings and transitional nature and any other matter consequent on or ancillary to the creation of the corporation.

content.txt: ch 4, pt 4, div 6: Subst 2010 No 133, Sch 2[59].

block.txt: A private water trust must for each year commencing on 1 July fix the rates and charges payable in respect of each landholding owned or occupied by its members that is a landholding for which the trust may exercise functions, or for which it provides water or drainage services in that year.
In determining the amount of rates and charges payable, the trust must fix an amount that it considers is sufficient to meet the estimated costs of the following—
the trust’s likely costs in providing irrigation, water supply, drainage and flood control services for that year,
the liabilities of the trust,
the likely costs relating to trust works, including (but not limited to) maintenance, improvement and replacement of works and new works,
provision for a sinking fund (if necessary),
any other matters prescribed by the regulations.
The rates and charges payable may (but are not required to) be fixed on the basis of any one or more of the following—
the volume or quality of water supplied or proposed to be supplied to a landholding,
the area of a landholding,
whether or not water or drainage services are or are proposed to be provided to a landholding,
the purpose for which water services are supplied or proposed to be supplied to a landholding.

If rates and charges are payable on the basis of the area of a landholding, a landholding that has an area equal to a number of hectares and a remaining fraction of a hectare is to be rounded up to the nearest hectare.
The trust may also fix the following charges—

termination charges payable by a member or former member in connection with the trust ceasing to supply water to the member or former member (whether because of the transformation of the member’s water entitlement to an access licence or otherwise),
charges payable for the delivery of water to a member after transformation of the whole or part of the member’s water entitlement.
A trust must give notice of its fees and charges for a year in the manner prescribed by the regulations and must specify in the notice the basis on which the rates and charges are calculated.
The rules of a trust must provide for the procedures for setting rates and charges and the period within which rates and charges must be paid.
The regulations may prescribe requirements for rules made under this section (see section 225 (3) (b)).

heading.b: Recovery of unpaid rates and charges

block.txt: The owner or occupier of a landholding for which rates or charges are levied by a private water trust must pay the rates and charges to the trust.
If a landholding for which rates or charges are levied is owned or occupied by more than one person the following provisions apply—
the rates or charges may be levied on one or more of those persons and may be recovered by the trust from any one or more of those persons,
the trust is not entitled to recover more than the total amount of the rates and charges (and any interest payable).

If any land in a holding reverts to the Crown during any year for which rates or charges are or are to be assessed, the person who immediately before the reversion was the landholder of the land is liable for payment of only that part of the rates or charges proportionate to the part of the year for which the land was held by the person, and any excess payment by the person must be refunded to the person.
Rates and charges are a charge on the land, procedures for the sale of land for overdue rates are set out in Part 4 of Chapter 7.
A private water trust may, in accordance with the rules, waive or reduce rates, charges and interest due.

Rates and charges may be waived under this section only if the auditor of the private water trust certifies that the waiver is in accordance with the rules and has been approved by the trustees of the trust.

content.txt: ch 4, pt 4, div 7: Ins 2010 No 133, Sch 2[59].

block.txt: A private water trust must cause proper accounts and records to be kept in relation to all the operations of the trust.
The trust must prepare financial statements for each financial year of the trust.

Section 7.6 of the Government Sector Finance Act 2018 applies to financial statements required to be prepared under this section in the same way that it applies to annual GSF financial statements required to be prepared under that Act.
The financial statements must be submitted for verification and certification to an auditor appointed in the manner prescribed by the rules of the trust.
The regulations may provide for the qualifications for appointment as an auditor under this section.
A trustee of a trust or a member of a trust must not be appointed to audit the financial statements of the trust.

heading.b: Auditor’s right to access to information

block.txt: An auditor of a private water trust has a right of access at all reasonable times to the accounts and records of the trust.

A trustee of a trust must comply with any reasonable request by the auditor of the trust to provide information or documents relating to the accounts or financial statements or related records of the trust.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A private water trust must, at the request of the Minister, furnish to the Minister the audited financial statements and any other documents requested within the time specified in the request.
The audited financial statement must be laid before the annual general meeting of the trust following their verification and certification by the auditor.
A private water trust has and may exercise the following functions—
to pay to the Treasury, at such times as may be fixed by the Minister, the interest and charges payable by the trust,
to borrow money, but only as provided by this section.

A loan by way of limited overdraft may be obtained for the purpose of meeting necessary legitimate expenditure prior to the collection of rates or for the purpose of carrying out urgent works of renewal, or replacement, or other emergency, for which sufficient funds are not immediately available.

On application by a trust the Minister may issue a certificate of limit of overdraft, in which must be named the purpose in respect of which the loan may be obtained and the limit of the amount to be borrowed.

The sum to be stated in the certificate as the limit of the overdraft is in the discretion of the Minister, but must not exceed the estimated amount required for the purpose mentioned therein plus 10% of such amount.

The loan is subject to any conditions inserted by the Minister in the certificate, and the money borrowed is taken to be secured on the income of the trust and must be repaid within the time fixed in the certificate.

All sums received on account of a trust’s sinking fund must be carried by the Treasurer to a special account, to be called “The Water Supply Loan Redemption Fund”, and all other sums to the Consolidated Fund.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to regulating the payment to the Crown of interest.

heading.b: Winding up of private water trusts

content.txt: ch 4, pt 4, div 8: Ins 2010 No 133, Sch 2[59].

block.txt: The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, remove the trustees of a private water trust from office and appoint an administrator to conduct the affairs of the trust.
The Minister may make an order if the Minister is of the opinion that—
the trustees or the trust have failed, or are unable to, carry out their functions as required by or under this Act, or
without limiting paragraph (a), the trustees or trust have failed or are unable to provide or maintain water supply, water distribution or drainage services or trust works, or
the trust is unable to pay its debts as they fall due, or
the trustees or trust have regularly or materially contravened this Act, the regulations or the rules of the trust, or
in all the circumstances of the case it is just and equitable to do so.
Before making an order, the Minister must—
cause notice of the proposed order to be published in a newspaper circulating in the local area in which the trust provides services, and
in that notice, invite submissions to be made to the Minister about the proposal within the period of 4 weeks following the publication of the notice, and
consider any submissions made within that period.
The Minister is not required to comply with subsection (3) if the Minister is of the opinion that the special circumstances of the case require the order to be made immediately.

The administrator of a private water trust appointed under this Division holds office for such period as is specified in the order appointing the administrator. The administrator ceases to hold office if the Minister, by a subsequent order published in the Gazette, revokes the appointment or on the appointment of new trustees under this section.

The administrator has and may exercise the functions of the trust specified in the administrator’s order of appointment (subject to any conditions specified in that order) but is not required to comply with the rules of the trust.
The administrator may amend the rules of the trust and take such other action as is necessary to enable the trust to properly exercise its functions.
The administrator is entitled to be paid such remuneration, from the funds of the trust, as the Minister may from time to time determine.
The Minister may at any time, by order published in the Gazette, extend the period of appointment of an administrator.
The administrator must, if required to do so by the Minister, report to the Minister on the administrator’s conduct of the affairs of the trust.
The administrator may at any time recommend to the Minister that new trustees be appointed or that the trust be wound up.
The administrator must, if required to do so by the Minister, arrange for elections to be held for new elected trustees.

heading.b: Removed trustees not eligible for re-election

block.txt: If the trustees of a private water trust have been removed from office, each of the trustees is ineligible for subsequent appointment or election as a trustee of the trust, unless the Minister declares in writing that the trustee is eligible for subsequent appointment or election.

heading.b: Effect of administration on existing contracts

block.txt: On the appointment of an administrator of a private water trust—
all contracts of employment by or on behalf of the trust are terminated, and
the administrator may terminate any contract for the provision of services to or by or on behalf of the trust.

heading.b: Winding up of private water trusts

block.txt: The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, order that a private water trust be wound up if—
requested to do so by the trustees after a resolution to wind up the trust was passed at a meeting of the trust by not less than 75% of the members of the trust, or
the administrator of the trust has recommended that the trust be wound up.
The order must appoint a person as the liquidator of the trust.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the winding up of a trust and for the disposal of residual assets held by or on behalf of the trust.
The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, abolish a trust if satisfied that the winding up of the trust under this section has been completed.

content.txt: ch 4, pt 4, div 9: Ins 2010 No 133, Sch 2[59].

heading.b: Liability for water source and other changes

block.txt: A private water trust, the trustees of a trust, any officer or employee of the trustees of a trust or a person acting under the direction of the trust, trustees, officer or employee is not subject to any action, liability, claim or demand arising—
from the unavailability of water, or
from the escape of water from a trust work, or
from a failure to supply, distribute or drain water that is authorised by the rules, this Act or the regulations,

as a consequence of anything done or omitted to be done in good faith by the trust, trustees, officer or employee or person for the purposes of executing this Act or of carrying out the functions of the trust.
This section does not limit section 397.
The Minister may, by notice in writing to a private water trust or the trustees of a trust, direct the trust or trustees to comply with, or cease to contravene, the rules of the trust.
The notice may direct the trust or trustees to take specified action or to cease to take specified action.
A trust or the trustees of a trust must not contravene a direction under this section.
Maximum penalty—Tier 2 penalty.
Maximum civil penalty—Tier C civil penalty.
The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, change the name of a private water trust, if the change has been approved by the voting members in accordance with the rules of the trust.

heading.b: Private trusts not NSW government agencies

block.txt: A private water trust is not a NSW government agency.

block.txt: This Part applies to and in respect of land in the Hunter Valley.
In this Part—
Hunter River includes all tributaries that, directly or indirectly, flow into the Hunter River, and includes the estuary of the Hunter River and all arms and branches of that estuary.

Hunter Valley means the catchment area of the Hunter River, and includes the land shown on the plan marked “DWR PLA No 20/2551” held by the Department, and also includes such other land as is declared by the regulations to form part of the Hunter Valley.

levee bank means a levee bank designed or intended for the purpose of or that could or might have the effect of excluding or partially excluding the waters of the Hunter River or waters overflowing from the Hunter River from any land.
protective works means works for the protection of any works vested in or otherwise under the control of a public authority—
against flooding by waters overflowing from the Hunter River, or
against the effects of any such flooding, or
against the effects of river bank erosion.
tree includes sapling and shrub.

heading.b: Restriction on use of lands adjacent to levee banks

block.txt: If a levee bank has been constructed adjacent to the Hunter River, the Minister may, by notice in writing to—
the landholder of the land on which the levee bank has been constructed, or
the landholder of any land adjacent to the levee bank, or
the landholder of the whole or any part of the land lying between the levee bank and the Hunter River,

impose such conditions and restrictions on the use of such levee bank or land as the Minister considers necessary or desirable to ensure the stability of the levee bank and in the interests of flood prevention or mitigation within the Hunter Valley generally.
The Minister may in the like manner revoke or vary any notice given in pursuance of this section.
If any landholder to whom such a notice has been given contravenes any condition or restriction imposed by the notice, the Minister—
may authorise any person to enter the land to which such notice relates, and to take such remedial measures on that land as the Minister considers necessary, and
may recover any cost incurred in so doing from the landholder in any court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due and owing to the Crown.

If under this section conditions or restrictions on the use of any levee bank or land are imposed by the Minister, the landholder of the levee bank or land is entitled to claim and be paid compensation for any loss sustained by reason of those conditions or restrictions.

heading.b: Construction of fences, structures and flood works

block.txt: A person must not—
construct any building, fence or structure in, on, or adjacent to, a levee bank, or
construct a flood work on a floodplain,
except with the consent of the Minister.
Maximum penalty—Tier 2 penalty.
Maximum civil penalty—Tier C civil penalty.
The Minister’s consent may be given unconditionally or subject to conditions.
An authorised officer—
may enter any lands on which any building, fence or flood work has been constructed otherwise than in accordance with the Minister’s consent, and
may take such measures as are necessary to demolish or remove the building, fence or flood work or to render the flood work ineffective.
The costs incurred by an authorised officer under this section are recoverable from the landholder as a debt in a court of competent jurisdiction.
The Minister may, by notice published in the Gazette, exclude any lands from a floodplain.

In this section, floodplain means any lands declared to be within the floodplain of the Hunter River by a proclamation in force under section 16 of the former Hunter Valley Flood Mitigation Act 1956, other than lands excluded from the floodplain by a notice published under this section.

heading.b: Accounts to be kept in Special Deposits Account

block.txt: There is to be established in the Special Deposits Account an account to be called the “Hunter Valley Flood Mitigation Account”.
Within the Hunter Valley Flood Mitigation Account is to be kept an account to be called the “Hunter Valley Flood Mitigation Working Account”, in this Part referred to as the Working Account.

Any amount paid to the Minister by Local Land Services is to be paid into the Working Account, from which account may be made, in such manner as the Treasurer determines, any payments that the Minister is required to make under or for the purposes of this Part.

This section applies to all flood works that are constructed or maintained by the Minister, other than those for which Local Land Services is liable to make contribution under some other provision of this Division.
Local Land Services is liable to contribute one-quarter of the cost to the Minister of constructing and maintaining any flood work to which this section applies.

heading.b: Cost of works to protect towns and villages

block.txt: This section applies to all flood works constructed or maintained by the Minister for the purpose of protecting a town or village from flooding, being works that have been constructed at the request or with the concurrence of the local council within whose area the town or village is situated.
Of the cost to the Minister of constructing and maintaining any flood work to which this section applies—
the local council is liable to contribute such percentage (not exceeding 12%) as the Minister may determine, and
Local Land Services is liable to contribute one-quarter of the balance.
Of the cost to the Minister of constructing and maintaining any protective works—
the public authority whose works are protected by the protective works is liable to contribute such percentage as the Minister may determine, and
Local Land Services is liable to contribute one-quarter of the balance.
The Minister may pay to any public authority that constructs or maintains any protective works such amount as the Minister considers appropriate towards the cost to the public authority of so doing.
Local Land Services is liable to pay to the Minister one-quarter of any amount paid to a public authority under subsection (2).

heading.b: Annual contribution to works program by Local Land Services

block.txt: Local Land Services is liable to pay to the Minister in each financial year—
one-quarter of the estimated cost of constructing any flood works that the Minister proposes to construct during that financial year, and
one-quarter of the estimated cost of maintaining any flood works that the Minister proposes to maintain during that financial year.
The following amounts are to be deducted from the estimated costs for the purpose of calculating Local Land Services’ liability under this section—
any contribution to those costs for which a local council will be liable under this Division,
any amount that Local Land Services has paid to the Minister under this section during the previous financial year but that remained unexpended at the end of that year.
Any estimates are to be made by the Minister whose decision is final.

heading.b: Consultation with Local Land Services as to works program

block.txt: Before the beginning of each financial year or as soon as practicable thereafter, the Minister must submit to Local Land Services a program of the flood works that the Minister proposes to construct or maintain during that year.
Such a program must be consistent with any management plan that applies to the land on which the works or proposed works are situated.
Such a program must be accompanied by a statement setting out the following particulars—
the estimated cost of constructing any work,
the estimated annual cost of maintaining any work,
the amount for which Local Land Services will be liable,
such other particulars as may be prescribed by the regulations.

heading.b: Consultation with local council as to works program

block.txt: This section applies to all flood works constructed or maintained by the Minister for the purpose of protecting a town or village from flooding, being works that have been constructed at the request or with the concurrence of the local council within whose area the town or village is situated.

Before the beginning of each financial year or as soon as practicable thereafter, the Minister must submit to the local council concerned a program of the flood works that the Minister proposes to construct or maintain during that year.
Such a program must be consistent with any management plan that applies to the land on which the works or proposed works are situated.
Such a program must be accompanied by a statement setting out the following particulars—
the estimated cost of constructing any work,
the estimated annual cost of maintaining any work,
the percentage that the Minister has determined that the council should contribute to the cost of the construction and maintenance of the work,
the amount for which the council will be liable,
such other particulars as may be prescribed by the regulations.
Any estimates are to be made by the Minister whose decision is final.
When the work has been completed, the Minister must notify the local council of the actual cost of the work.
If the amount paid by the local council in respect of the work is more than the amount for which the council is liable, the Minister must repay to the council the amount of such excess.
If the amount paid by the local council in respect of the work is less than the amount for which the council is liable, the council must pay to the Minister the amount of the shortfall.
Any amount paid to the Minister by a local council under this section is to be paid into the Hunter Valley Flood Mitigation Working Account.

heading.b: Payment of contribution towards maintenance by a local council

block.txt: A local council that is liable to contribute to the cost of maintenance of any flood work must pay to the Minister in each financial year the same percentage of the estimated cost of maintenance as the council is liable to contribute to the actual cost of maintenance of that work.

In calculating the local council’s liability under this subsection in respect of any financial year there is to be deducted any amount that the council has paid to the Minister in respect of any flood work during any previous financial year and that remained unexpended at the end of the immediately preceding financial year.
Any estimate is to be made by the Minister whose decision is final.

heading.b: Consultation with local council as to maintenance program

block.txt: Before the beginning of each financial year, the Minister must furnish the local council with a statement setting out the following particulars—
the amount that the council will be liable to pay under this Division for that financial year,
such other particulars as may be prescribed by the regulations.
The local council must pay to the Minister the amount referred to in subsection (1) (a).
Any such amount is to be paid into the Hunter Valley Flood Mitigation Working Account.

If in the opinion of the Minister it becomes necessary to carry out urgent maintenance on any flood work, the Minister may carry out the maintenance, despite maintenance not having been included in any program of works or any statement furnished to a local council.

When the maintenance has been completed, the Minister must determine the total amount paid in respect of such maintenance and notify any local council affected by the work and Local Land Services of the respective amounts that they are required to contribute in accordance with this Division.
Any money paid to the Minister under this section is to be paid into the Hunter Valley Flood Mitigation Working Account.
Any amount that is payable to the Minister under this Division—
by Local Land Services, or
by a local council, or
by any other public authority,
is payable at such times, and in such instalments, as the Minister may determine.

heading.b: Works to protect public and local government works to be approved by Minister

block.txt: A public authority must not construct any protective works unless the Minister has approved of the site, nature, dimensions and design of the works.

In giving approval, the Minister may require such amendment of the site, nature, dimensions or design of the protective works as the Minister considers necessary, and the public authority must comply with that requirement accordingly.

The Minister may by notice in writing require the public authority by which any protective works have been constructed to take specified measures for the proper upkeep, preservation and maintenance of the protective works.
The public authority must comply with the requirements specified in the notice in such manner and within such time as is so specified.
If a public authority fails to comply with the terms of the notice, the Minister—
may authorise any person to enter the land on which the protective works are located and carry out the measures specified in such notice, and
may recover any cost incurred in so doing from the public authority in any court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due to the Crown.

heading.b: Major floodgates to be maintained and operated by local councils

block.txt: If in the opinion of the Minister any floodgate operates for the protection of lands other than lands owned by one landholder or a small localised group of landholders, the Minister may by notice in writing to the local council declare the floodgate to be a major floodgate.
It is the duty of the local council—
to keep any major floodgate at all times in a good and proper state of repair and working order, and
to maintain and operate it in accordance with any directions that may from time to time be given by the Minister.
If the local council fails to perform that duty, the Minister—

may authorise any person to enter the land on which the major floodgate is located and to take such measures as to the maintenance, operation or repair of the floodgate as the Minister considers necessary, and
may recover any cost incurred in so doing from the council in any court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due to the Crown.
In this section, minor floodgate means any floodgate that is not a major floodgate.
It is the duty of each landholder for the protection of whose land a minor floodgate operates to keep the floodgate at all times in a good and proper state of repair and working order.

If any such landholder fails to perform that duty, the Minister may by notice in writing direct the landholder to take such measures as to the maintenance, operation or repair of the floodgate as may be specified in the notice.
If any landholder fails to comply with the terms of the notice, the Minister—

may authorise any person to enter the land on which the minor floodgate is located and to take such measures as to the maintenance, operation or repair of the floodgate as the Minister considers necessary, and
may recover any cost incurred in so doing from the landholder in any court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due to the Crown.

In the case of multiple landholders, the liability imposed on them under this section is joint and several but, as between themselves, each is liable only for such share of the liability as bears the same proportion to the total liability as the area of the person’s land for the protection of which the floodgate operates bears to the total area of land for the protection of which the floodgate operates.
If any landholder pays to the Minister more than the person’s share of the total liability the landholder may recover the excess by way of contribution from the others.
Sections 91–95 of the Public Works Act 1912 do not apply to any works constructed under this Part.
If the Minister is empowered to recover any cost incurred in carrying out any work or measure, a certificate by the Minister of the amount of such cost is evidence of that cost.
This Part applies to each body referred to in Schedule 2 (referred to as a major utility).
The Governor may by proclamation published on the NSW legislation website amend Schedule 2 so as—
to add the corporate name of any body that is to become a major utility for the purposes of this Part, or
to vary the name of any major utility as a consequence of any change in its corporate name, or
to omit the corporate name of any body.

heading.b: Review of activities of major utilities

block.txt: The activities of a major utility under this Act—
may be reviewed at any time, and
must be reviewed—
before the end of the 6 month period following the date on which its first approval was granted under section 95, and
before the end of each 5 year period following the date on which its current approval was granted.
For the purpose of conducting such a review, the Minister must cause notice to be published—
in the Gazette, and
in the authorised manner,
inviting written submissions from interested persons in relation to the activities of the major utility during the period under review.
In this Part—
area of operations of a water supply authority means the area of operations prescribed by the regulations in relation to that authority.
charging year, in relation to a water supply authority, means—
the period of 12 months declared by an order in force under Division 6 to be the charging year for the water supply authority, or
if the charging year is changed under that Division by a further order, the period between the end of one charging year and the beginning of the next.
development area means an area of land declared by an order in force under Division 6 to be a development area.
discharge approval—see section 300A(4).
drainage area means an area of land declared by an order in force under Division 6 to be a drainage area.
drainage service means that part of drainage pipework up to its point of connection to a water supply authority’s drainage system.
drainage service pipe means a pipe connecting a drainage service to a water supply authority’s drainage system, and includes the plumbing fittings connected to the pipe.
floodplain means an area of land declared by an order in force under Division 6 to be a floodplain.
meter includes any measuring device.
plumbing fitting includes any pipe, apparatus or fixture used for plumbing work.
plumbing work means work comprising or affecting—
a water supply service pipe or its connection (whether directly or indirectly) with a water supply authority’s water supply system, or
a sewerage service pipe or its connection (whether directly or indirectly) with a water supply authority’s sewerage system, or
a drainage service pipe or its connection (whether directly or indirectly) with a water supply authority’s drainage system.
river management area means an area of land declared by an order in force under Division 6 to be a river management area.
service charge means any of the following—
a water service charge,
a sewerage service charge,
a drainage service charge,
a loan service charge,
a developmental works service charge,
a flood mitigation service charge,
a river management service charge, or
a special industry service charge,
that may be levied under Division 6.
sewage work means a work (such as a pump, pipe or channel) for the purpose of removing sewage or other waste matter from land, including a reticulated system of such works, and includes—
all associated pipes, valves, pumps and other equipment, and
all sewage treatment or sewage processing plants and their outfalls and drainage beds,
but does not include any work declared by the regulations not to be a sewage work.
sewerage service means that part of sewerage pipework, including all sanitary fixtures, up to its point of connection to a water supply authority’s sewerage system.
sewerage service pipe means a pipe connecting a sewerage service to a water supply authority’s sewerage system, and includes the plumbing fittings connected to the pipe.
special area means an area of land declared under Division 4 to be a special area.
special industry means an industry declared by an order in force under Division 6 to be a special industry.

water management work means a water supply work, drainage work, sewage work or flood work, and includes a work in the nature of a water supply work (being a work that receives water from a water supply work under the control or management of a water supply authority).
water supply service means that part of water supply pipework from its point of connection to a water supply authority’s water supply system up to and including its outlet valves.
water supply service pipe means a pipe connecting a water supply service to a water supply authority’s water supply system, and includes the plumbing fittings connected to the pipe.
water supply work includes any work that receives water from a water supply work under the control or management of a water supply authority.

heading.b: Requirements for access licences and approvals

block.txt: Nothing in this Part authorises a water supply authority to do anything for which this Act requires an access licence or approval unless the water supply authority holds an appropriate access licence or approval.
The corporations listed in Schedule 3 are water supply authorities.
A corporation listed in Part 1 of Schedule 3 is, for the purposes of any Act, a statutory body representing the Crown.
The Governor may, by proclamation published on the NSW legislation website—
name a water supply authority proposed to be constituted under this section, and
specify the number of members, the qualification for each member and whether or not the member is a full-time member or a part-time member, and
amend Schedule 3 by adding the name of the water supply authority to Part 1 of that Schedule.
The members are to be appointed by the Governor and, on their appointment, the water supply authority is constituted as a corporation.
The corporate name for the water supply authority is the name of the water supply authority stated in the proclamation.

On a change of area of operations or functions for a water supply authority listed in Part 1 of Schedule 3, the Governor may, by proclamation published in the Gazette, do either or both of the following—
change the number of part-time members of the water supply authority,
change the qualifications for part-time members of the water supply authority.
A change referred to in subsection (4) does not affect the identity of the water supply authority.

heading.b: Statutory body may be water supply authority

block.txt: The Governor may, by proclamation published on the NSW legislation website with the consent of the Minister administering the Act by or under which a statutory body is constituted, amend Schedule 3 by adding the name of the statutory body to Part 2 of that Schedule.
On the addition of the name of a statutory body to Part 2 of Schedule 3, it becomes a water supply authority but still has its other functions.

heading.b: Provisions relating to constitution and procedure of water supply authorities

block.txt: Part 1 of Schedule 5 has effect with respect to the members of the water supply authorities listed in Part 1 of Schedule 3.
Part 2 of Schedule 5 has effect with respect to the Australian Inland Energy Water Infrastructure.
Part 3 of Schedule 5 has effect with respect to the Cobar Water Board.
Parts 2 and 3 of Schedule 5 do not affect the operation of the other provisions of this Part in relation to the water supply authorities to which those Parts relate.
The area of operations of a water supply authority is such as may be prescribed by the regulations for the water supply authority.
If a regulation so provides, a water supply authority has, and may exercise, in its area of operations or a specified part of its area of operations—
only such of the functions of a water supply authority as are specified in the regulation, or
all functions of a water supply authority other than functions specified in the regulation.
A regulation made for the purposes of subsection (2) may make provision for or with respect to—
matters affecting revenue, assets, rights, liabilities and employees of a water supply authority, and
procedures to be adopted for the purposes of paragraph (a).
Within the area of operations of a water supply authority, a function under this Part may be exercised only by the water supply authority unless—
the function is exercisable by the Minister, or
the function is exercised by Local Land Services under the Local Land Services Act 2013, or
with the consent of the Minister, the function is exercised by another Minister, by the delegate of another Minister or by a statutory body, or
this Part provides otherwise.
With the consent of the Minister, a water supply authority may exercise a function outside its area of operations.
Until a regulation is made for the purposes of subsection (1), the area of operations of a water supply authority is the same as it was immediately before the commencement of this Part.
Persons may be employed in the Public Service under the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 to enable a corporation listed in Part 1 of Schedule 3 to exercise its functions.

Section 59 of the Government Sector Employment Act 2013 provides that the persons so employed (or whose services a water supply authority makes use of) may be referred to as officers or employees, or members of staff, of the water supply authority. Section 47A of the Constitution Act 1902 precludes a water supply authority from employing staff.
A water supply authority may delegate to a person the exercise of any of its functions, other than this power of delegation.
A water supply authority has the following functions—
subject to the Minister’s approval, to construct, maintain and operate water management works and other associated works,
to conduct research, collect information and develop technology in relation to water management,
to do anything for the purpose of enabling the objects of this Act to be attained.
A water supply authority may exercise its functions within and beyond its area of operations.
A water supply authority must not exercise any function beyond its area of operations in such a way as to limit its capacity to exercise that function within that area.
It is the duty of a water supply authority to exercise its functions consistently with the principles of ecologically sustainable development.
The regulations may make further provision about the approval of the Minister under subsection (1)(a).

heading.b: Exercise of functions by a water supply authority

block.txt: A water supply authority—
has and may exercise the functions conferred or imposed on it by or under this or any other Act, and
in the exercise of its functions (except in relation to the contents of a report or recommendation made by it) is subject to the control and direction of the Minister.
Subsection (1) (b) does not apply to a water supply authority listed in Part 3 of Schedule 3.

If a function conferred or imposed on a water supply authority by this Part is inconsistent with a function conferred or imposed on the water supply authority by or under another Act, this Part prevails.
With the approval of the Governor, a water supply authority may enter into commercial operations with respect to—
any services developed in connection with the exercise of its functions, or
any products or by-products (including intellectual property) resulting from the exercise of its functions, or
such other matters as may be prescribed by the regulations.
With the approval of the Governor, a water supply authority may form, or join in forming, a company, partnership or trust for the purpose of exercising its functions under this Part.

A water supply authority may, at the request of a statutory body and with the consent of the Minister, exercise any of the functions of the statutory body in a part of its area of operations in respect of which the statutory body may exercise different functions, even if, but for the request, the water supply authority would not have exercised the function.

heading.b: Entry on land to read meters or carry out works

block.txt: A water supply authority may, by its employees and agents—
enter and occupy land and there exercise any of its functions, including the carrying out of any work on, below or above the surface of the land, and
divert water from, or alter the course of, a stream, and
impound or take water on, in or under the surface of any land.

The power conferred by this section is sufficient authority for an employee or agent to enter and occupy land or any part of a building (except an enclosed part occupied as a separate dwelling) in the exercise of a water supply authority’s functions during daylight for the purpose of—
reading a meter, or
ascertaining whether trade waste is present or is being (or has recently been) discharged to a work of the authority, or
making a valuation,
unless the employee or agent is refused access by the lawful occupier of the land.
A water supply authority may, in accordance with the regulations, attach a ventilating shaft, pipe or tube for a sewer to the wall of a building.
A water supply authority may remove or use anything dug up or obtained in the exercise of its powers under this section.
A water supply authority—
must do as little damage as practicable in exercising its powers under this section, and
must compensate all persons who suffer damage by the exercise of the powers,
in relation to the land entered.
Compensation may be made by reinstatement or repair, by construction of works or by payment.
If a water supply authority provides a sewer, compensation is required only if—
the sewer causes injury to, or interference with, a building or other structure, or
a manhole or main ventilator is constructed on the land.
A claim for compensation—
is ineffective unless made in writing not later than 6 months after the damage was suffered, and
in the absence of agreement on the compensation, must be dealt with as if it were a claim for compensation for the acquisition of land for public purposes under the Public Works Act 1912.
A water supply authority may at any time, by its employees or agents, enter any land (except an enclosed part occupied as a separate dwelling) for the purpose of finding out—
the character and condition of the land or building, or
the condition or location of any water management work used in connection with the land or building, or
whether any use, consumption, waste, misuse or undue consumption of water supplied by a water supply authority is occurring, or
whether any offence against this Act has been, or is being, committed.
A water supply authority must not exercise the powers conferred by subsection (1) unless—
reasonable written notice of its intention to do so has first been given to the landholder of the land, building or dwelling house, or
it authorises the entry after forming the opinion that the giving of the notice would cause undue delay.
Reasonable force may be used to enter land, or a building other than a dwelling house, under this section.
If the powers of entry under this section are exercised—
without notice being given, or
by force,
the water supply authority must, without delay, notify such persons as it considers appropriate of the action taken.

The water supply authority may, by notice in writing given to the landholder of the land or building, require all defective or improper work discovered on an inspection to be repaired, altered or removed within 24 hours or such longer period as is stated in the notice.

If a notice under subsection (5) is not complied with, the water supply authority may, by its employees and agents, enter the land, building or dwelling house and repair, alter or remove the defective or improper work.
If a notice is given under subsection (5)—
the costs and expenses of the entry and inspection by the water supply authority, and
if the notice is not complied with, the costs and expenses of the water supply authority in acting under subsection (6),
are recoverable from the landholder as a service charge.
If, on an inspection under this section—
no defective or improper work is discovered, and
no waste, misuse or undue consumption of water supplied by the water supply authority is occurring, and
no offence against this Act is discovered,
the water supply authority must make good any damage or disturbance caused by it for the purposes of the inspection.
In exercising its powers under this section, a water supply authority must do as little damage as practicable.
A water supply authority may, on giving reasonable notice to persons likely to be affected, open and break up—
the soil and pavement of a public road or public reserve, and
any sewer, drain or tunnel in or under a public road or public reserve,
for the purpose of exercising its functions.

The statutory body having the control and management of a public road or public reserve may, as prescribed by the regulations, require a water supply authority to comply with conditions in exercising its powers under subsection (1), including conditions for restoration of the surface and removal of rubbish.

If a public road or public reserve is damaged by a leakage from, or a bursting of, a water supply authority’s water main or sewer main, the statutory body having the control and management of the public road or public reserve may require the water supply authority to make good the damage without delay.
If a water supply authority fails—
to comply with a condition in force under subsection (2), or
to comply with a requirement under subsection (3),
the statutory body affected by the failure may remedy it and recover the cost of doing so as a debt owed to the statutory body by the water supply authority.
If—
a water supply authority, in order to exercise its functions, needs an alteration to be made in the position of a conduit owned by another person, and
the alteration would not permanently damage the conduit or adversely affect its operation,
the water supply authority may serve on the person a written notice that complies with subsection (2).
A notice must—
specify the alteration needed, and
require the alteration to be made within a reasonable time stated in the notice, and
include an undertaking by the water supply authority to pay the reasonable cost of the alteration.

If the alteration is not made as required by the notice, the water supply authority may make the alteration in such a manner as not to damage the conduit permanently or adversely affect its operation on completion of the alteration.

In this section, conduit means anything that is in or under a public road (or any other land on which no building or other structure is located) and is used for the conveyance of a substance, energy or signals.
If a person places a structure or other thing in or near a water supply authority’s water management work in such a manner as to interfere with the work, the water supply authority may—
demolish and remove the structure or other thing, and
repair the work, and
recover the cost of doing so as a debt owing to the water supply authority by the person who placed the structure or other thing there.
A water supply authority may apply for and obtain an injunction to prevent a structure or other thing being placed as referred to in subsection (1).

heading.b: Discharges into sewerage and drainage systems

block.txt: A water supply authority must not grant a discharge approval unless it is in accordance with—
the regulations, and
the water supply authority’s discharge policy.
A water supply authority’s discharge policy—
must be made in accordance with the regulations, and
may specify the kinds of substances that do not require a discharge approval or for which a discharge approval must not be granted.
The regulations may make provision about the following—
the regulation and prohibition of the discharge of substances into a water supply authority’s sewerage system or drainage system,
discharge approvals,
discharge policies, including—
that the Minister may determine matters that must be addressed in a discharge policy, and
the circumstances in which the Minister’s approval of a discharge policy is required.
In this section—
discharge approval means an approval to discharge substances into a water supply authority’s sewerage system.
discharge policy, of a water supply authority, means a policy about the discharge of substances into the water supply authority’s sewerage system.

heading.b: Finding source of pollution of water supply

block.txt: If water supplied by a water supply authority is being polluted, the water supply authority may, after giving reasonable notice to persons likely to be affected by its action, dig up the ground and try to find the source of the pollution.
If it is found that a person given notice under this section is not responsible for the pollution, the water supply authority must bear the expenses of—
the digging, examination, repair and reinstatement of the broken ground, and
the repair of any damage caused by the water supply authority to the property of the person.
A water supply authority may recover the expenses incurred by it as a debt due to the water supply authority by any person responsible for the pollution.

Without limiting Part 1 of Chapter 7, the Minister’s power to give directions under that Part may be exercised in relation to a water supply authority’s sewage work as if it were a water management work within the meaning of that Part.

An appeal lies to the Land and Environment Court against the Minister’s decision to give such a direction in the same way as it lies against the Minister’s decision to give a direction under Part 1 of Chapter 7.

heading.b: Regulations for protection of water supply

block.txt: The regulations may make provision about—
the regulation and prohibition of activities to protect the supply or quality of water, and
the functions of a water supply authority in protecting the supply of water.

heading.b: Regulations for measurement of supply of water

block.txt: The regulations may make provision about the measurement of water supplied by a water supply authority, including the following—
the method of measurement,
information to be provided by persons about the supply,
requirements for persons to meter the water supplied,
the installation, location, care, maintenance, testing and discontinuance of meters,
faulty meters, including adjustments in fees or charges for faulty meters,
directions given by water supply authorities to persons about matters referred to in paragraphs (a)–(d),
the ownership of meters on land not vested in a water supply authority.
The regulations may make provision about the following—
the notification of drainage areas and charges,
the mapping of drainage areas by water supply authorities,
the objections to being included within a drainage area,
the adjudication of the objections and the binding nature of the adjudication.

heading.b: Regulations for firefighting water supply services and fire hydrants

block.txt: The regulations may make provision about firefighting water supply services and fire-hydrants, including the following—
the installation, maintenance and use of firefighting water supply services,
directions given by water supply authorities to persons about firefighting water supply services, including about matters referred to in paragraph (a),
the installation, use, maintenance and removal of fire hydrants by water supply authorities or persons authorised by a water supply authority,
the supply of water by water supply authorities for the purpose of controlling and extinguishing fires, including the supply of water to fire hydrants.
In this section—
firefighting water supply service means the part of a water supply service designed to be used for controlling and extinguishing fires.
The Governor may, on the recommendation of the Minister, by order published in the Gazette, declare an area of land described in the order to be a special area for a water supply authority.
The Minister may recommend an order only if of the opinion that the exercise of the State’s water rights could be adversely affected unless the order is made.
Action may not be taken under the Crown Land Management Act 2016 in respect of land within a special area for a water supply authority unless—
a water supply authority has given its approval in writing, and
any conditions to which the approval is subject are complied with.
A water supply authority may, in a special area, exercise the functions of a Crown land manager under the Crown Land Management Act 2016 without being appointed as such.

heading.b: Exercise of certain functions in special areas

block.txt: A public agency may not, in relation to land within a special area for a water supply authority, exercise functions other than functions under this Part unless notice is first given, as prescribed by the regulations, to the water supply authority.
On receipt of such a notice, the water supply authority may make such representations to the public agency as it thinks fit.
A public agency may not exercise functions contrary to any such representations made by a water supply authority unless—
at least 14 days’ notice has been given to the water supply authority of the functions intended to be exercised, and
that period has expired without the matter being referred to the Minister as a dispute for determination.
In this section, public agency means—
the Governor, or
a Minister of the Crown, or
a statutory body.
The regulations may make provision about special areas, including the following—
the regulation and prohibition of the following—
the extraction, use, pollution or contamination of waters within the areas,
the pollution or contamination of land within the areas,
access to, or the use of, the areas,
other conduct in relation to the areas,
the circumstances and way in which a water supply authority may regulate, prohibit or consent to conduct referred to in paragraph (a)(i)–(iv),
the persons authorised, or the circumstances and way in which persons may be authorised, to manage and protect the areas (authorised persons),
the functions of authorised persons,
directions given by authorised persons, including the giving of directions to persons about—
conduct referred to in paragraph (a)(i)–(iv),
the surrender or inspection of things for, or the investigation of, contraventions or suspected contraventions of this Act or the regulations.

A regulation made under this Act about a special area prevails to the extent of an inconsistency with a statutory instrument made under another Act, other than a State environmental planning policy made under the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979.

heading.b: Developer contributions to the construction of works

block.txt: A person may apply to a water supply authority for a certificate of compliance for development carried out, or proposed to be carried out, within the water supply authority’s area.
An application must be accompanied by such information as the regulations may prescribe.

heading.b: Authority may impose certain requirements before granting certificate of compliance

block.txt: This section applies to such kinds of development as are prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this section.

As a precondition to granting a certificate of compliance for development, a water supply authority may, by notice in writing served on the applicant, require the applicant to do either or both of the following—

to pay a specified amount to the water supply authority by way of contribution towards the cost of such water management works as are specified in the notice, being existing works or projected works, or both,
to construct water management works to serve the development.
In calculating an amount for the purposes of subsection (2) (a)—
the value of existing water management works and the estimated cost of projected water management works may be taken into consideration, and
the amount of any government subsidy or similar payment is not to be deducted from the relevant value or cost of the water management works, and
consideration is to be given to any guidelines issued for the time being for the purposes of this section by the Minister.

If a water supply authority imposes a requirement under this section on the Crown, the Crown may request the Minister for Urban Affairs and Planning to determine whether such a requirement should be imposed and, if so, in what terms.
The determination made by the Minister for Urban Affairs and Planning in response to such a request is final and is taken to be the determination of the water supply authority.
Any water management works constructed in compliance with a requirement under this section are the property of the water supply authority.
A water supply authority must grant a certificate of compliance for development—
within 60 days after an application for the granting of such a certificate is made, or
if, within that period, the water supply authority imposes a requirement on the applicant under this Division, as soon as it is satisfied that the requirement has been complied with.

A water supply authority may be satisfied that a requirement under this Division has been complied with if the applicant lodges with the water supply authority such security for compliance with the requirement as the water supply authority may approve.

If a water supply authority fails or refuses to give a compliance certificate within the period of 60 days after an application is duly made in that regard, the applicant may appeal to the Land and Environment Court, within 12 months after the expiration of that period, against the failure or refusal.

heading.b: Orders for purpose of service charges

block.txt: The Governor may, by order published in the Gazette, declare any land described in the order to be a development area for the purposes of this Part.
The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, declare any land described in the order to be a drainage area, floodplain or river management area for the purposes of this Part.
The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, declare any industry specified in the order to be a special industry for the purposes of this Part.
The Minister may, by order published in the Gazette, declare a period of 12 months to be the charging year for a water supply authority.
On a water supply authority’s water main or a sewer main becoming available for connection, the water supply authority may—
publish in the Gazette notice of its availability, and
