An order to give a financial assurance ceases to have effect if the Regulator gives the offender written notice that the project or activity to which the financial assurance relates has been completed satisfactorily.

The offender is liable for anything done or omitted to be done in good faith by the Regulator under section 353K(1) in connection with the carrying out or completion of the relevant project or activity.

heading.b: Financial assurance does not affect other penalty or charge

block.txt: A financial assurance may be claimed or realised despite, and without affecting—
other action that might be taken or is required to be taken in relation to a contravention or other circumstances to which the assurance relates.

heading.b: Disputes about calling on or using financial assurance

block.txt: The Land and Environment Court has jurisdiction to determine disputes about claiming or realising financial assurances.
The regulations may provide for the following—
the form and amount of a financial assurance required to be given,
the way the Regulator may make a claim or realise a financial assurance,
the giving of notice for this part.

heading.b: Recovery of rates, charges and other money

content.txt: ch 7, pt 4, hdg: Subst 2004 No 39, Sch 4 [42].

heading.b: Recovery of rates, charges and other amounts by charging authorities

content.txt: ch 7, pt 4, div 1, hdg: Ins 2004 No 39, Sch 4 [42].

block.txt: In this Part, charging authority means the Minister, an irrigation corporation, a private water corporation, a private water trust or a water supply authority.

heading.b: Certain rates and charges to be a charge on land

block.txt: A rate or charge imposed on the owner of any land is a charge on the land to which the charge relates.
A charge imposed for a service or thing supplied or provided in connection with a specific parcel of land is a charge on the land.
The provisions of this section have effect despite anything contained in section 42 of the Real Property Act 1900.
A charging authority may charge interest on overdue rates and charges at a rate not exceeding the rate of interest payable for the time being on an unpaid judgment of the Supreme Court.

heading.b: Recovery of rates, charges and other money

block.txt: Any rate or charge or other money due to a charging authority under this Act may be recovered in any court of competent jurisdiction as if it were a debt due to the charging authority.
An unsatisfied judgment or order of any court for the recovery of any rate or charge from any person is not a bar to its recovery from any other person who is liable under this Act for its payment.

If land is owned or held jointly by two or more persons, such persons are jointly and severally liable to the charging authority for the rate, but as between themselves each are only be liable for such part of the rate as is proportionate to his or her interest in the land.
If any of such persons pays to the charging authority more than his or her proportionate part, he or she may recover the excess by way of contribution from the others.

heading.b: Sale of land for unpaid rates and charges

block.txt: This section applies to rates and charges imposed under this Act by the Minister or by a water supply authority, private water corporation or private water trust.

The provisions of Division 5 of Part 2 of Chapter 17 of the Local Government Act 1993 apply to land in respect of which a rate or charge (being a rate or charge that is, by virtue of this Part, a charge on land) remains unpaid in the same way as they apply to land in respect of which rates and charges under that Act remain unpaid.
For the purpose of applying the provisions of Division 5 of Part 2 of Chapter 17 of the Local Government Act 1993 to land in respect of which a rate or charge remains unpaid—
a reference in those provisions to a council is to be read as a reference to the Minister or to a water supply authority, private water corporation or private water trust, as the case requires, and

a reference to a general manager or public officer is to be read as a reference to the Secretary or to the principal officer of a water supply authority, private water corporation or private water trust, as the case requires, and

a reference to a member of staff of a council is to be read as a reference to a member of staff of the Department or to an employee of a water supply authority, private water corporation or private water trust, as the case requires, and
a reference to a rating authority is to be read as including a reference to a council.
A charging authority must, on written application being made to it and payment of the fee determined by it, issue to the applicant a certificate—
containing particulars of any amounts payable to the authority in respect of a parcel of separately assessed land, or
to the effect that there are no such amounts.
An application for a certificate must—
specify the name and address of the applicant, and
identify the land to which the application relates.

Such a certificate is conclusive proof, in favour of a purchaser in good faith and for value of the land to which the certificate relates that, at the date of its issue, no amounts were payable to the charging authority in respect of that land other than such amounts as are specified in the certificate.

heading.b: Liability where an estate or interest is transferred

block.txt: A person who disposes of his or her estate or interest in any land in respect of which any rates or charges have been or may be levied remains liable for rates or charges to the same extent as if the person had not disposed of his or her estate or interest in the land, if the rates or charges are levied either—
before the person disposed of his or her estate or interest in the land, or
before the person has given to the charging authority the prescribed notice of disposal.

If any person who disposes of land to another person pays any amount to the charging authority in respect of rates or charges levied after the land disposed of but before the prescribed notice is given to the authority, the person by whom the amount was paid may recover the amount from the person to whom the land was disposed.

As between an owner of land and any other person from or to whom the owner derives or disposes of his or her estate or interest in the land, rates or charges under this Act are to be considered as accruing from day to day and are apportionable accordingly.

heading.b: Liability where a person becomes entitled to an estate or interest

block.txt: An owner of land is liable for all arrears of rates and charges owing by any previous owner of the land, despite the fact that the new owner acquired the land after the rates or charges were levied.

If any person who becomes an owner of land pays to the charging authority any rates or charges in respect of that land that were levied before the person became the owner, the person may recover from the previous owner such part of the rates or charges as was levied in respect of the period during which the previous owner was the owner of the land.

content.txt: ch 7, pt 4, div 2, hdg: Ins 2004 No 39, Sch 4 [43].

block.txt: If an access licence is co-held by two or more co-holders, those co-holders are jointly and severally liable to the Minister for the fees, charges and administrative penalties relating to the licence, but as between themselves each are only liable for such part of those fees, charges and administrative penalties as is proportionate to his or her interest in the licence.
If any of those co-holders pays to the Minister more than his or her proportionate part, he or she may recover the excess by way of contribution from the others.

heading.b: Certificate as to charges outstanding in relation to access licences

block.txt: The Minister may, in relation to any access licence, issue a certificate to the effect that, as at the date on which the certificate is issued—
a specified amount is payable in relation to the access licence pursuant to fees, charges and administrative penalties imposed under this Act, or
no amount is so payable.

Such a certificate is conclusive proof that, as at the date on which it was issued, no amounts were payable in respect of the access licence other than such amounts as are specified in the certificate.

heading.b: Unpaid fees, charges and administrative penalties

block.txt: An administrative penalty imposed by the Minister under this Act that remains unpaid is recoverable in any court of competent jurisdiction as a debt due to the Crown.

If a fee, charge or administrative penalty imposed by the Minister under this Act relates to an access licence, the fee, charge or administrative penalty may be recovered from the holder of the licence who incurred the fee, charge or penalty or the holder of the licence for the time being.

Despite subsection (2), if a person surrenders an access licence, any fee, charge or administrative penalty imposed by the Minister under this Act that relates to the licence may be recovered from that person.
If a corporation commits an offence against this Act or the regulations—
each person who is a director of the corporation, and
each person who is concerned in the management of the corporation,
is taken to have committed the same offence if the person knowingly authorised or permitted the act or omission constituting the offence.
A person may be proceeded against and convicted under this section whether or not the corporation has been proceeded against or convicted.
Nothing in this section affects any liability imposed on a corporation for an offence committed by the corporation.

heading.b: Offences by joint holders of access licence or approval

block.txt: If an offence against this Act or the regulations arises in relation to an access licence or approval, each co-holder of the licence or approval is taken to have committed the offence.
A co-holder of a licence or approval is not guilty of such an offence if the co-holder establishes that—
the offence was committed by some other person (whether or not another co-holder of the licence or approval), and
the other person was not associated with the co-holder at the time the offence was committed, and
the co-holder took all reasonable steps to prevent the offence from being committed.

A person is associated with a co-holder of a licence or approval for the purposes of subsection (2) (b) (but without limiting any other circumstances of association) if the person is an employee, agent, licensee, contractor or sub-contractor of the co-holder.
A person may, under this section, be proceeded against and convicted for an offence whether or not any other person has been proceeded against or convicted for the offence.
For the purposes of this Act—
a Tier 1 penalty corresponds to a maximum penalty of—
in the case of a corporation, 45,500 penalty units and, in the case of a continuing offence, a further penalty of 2,400 penalty units for each day the offence continues, or

in any other case, imprisonment for 2 years or 10,000 penalty units, or both, and, in the case of a continuing offence, a further penalty of 1,200 penalty units for each day the offence continues, and
a Tier 2 penalty corresponds to a maximum penalty of—
in the case of a corporation, 18,200 penalty units and, in the case of a continuing offence, a further penalty of 1,200 penalty units for each day the offence continues, or
in any other case, 4,550 penalty units and, in the case of a continuing offence, a further penalty of 600 penalty units for each day the offence continues, and
a Tier 3 penalty corresponds to a maximum penalty of 100 penalty units.
Proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations are to be disposed of summarily—
by the Local Court, or
by the Land and Environment Court in its summary jurisdiction.
Proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations may be commenced at any time within, but not later than, 3 years after the date on which the offence is alleged to have been committed.

Proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations may also be commenced at any time within, but not later than, 3 years after the date on which evidence of the alleged offence first came to the attention of any relevant authorised officer.

If subsection (3) is relied on for the purpose of commencing proceedings for an offence, the process by which the proceedings are commenced must contain particulars of the date on which evidence of the offence first came to the attention of any relevant authorised officer and need not contain particulars of the date on which the offence was committed.

The date on which evidence first came to the attention of any relevant authorised officer is the date specified in the process by which the proceedings are commenced, unless the contrary is established.
The maximum monetary penalty that may be imposed by the Local Court in proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations is—
for a corporation—2,000 penalty units, or
otherwise—1,000 penalty units.
For a continuing offence, the Local Court may also impose a penalty of up to 10% of the further monetary penalty specified for the offence for each day the offence continues.
The maximum penalty that may be imposed by the Land and Environment Court in proceedings for an offence against this Act or the regulations is the maximum penalty specified in respect of the offence.
In this section, evidence of an offence means evidence of any act or omission constituting the offence.

heading.b: Matters to be considered in imposing penalty

block.txt: In imposing a penalty on a person for an offence against this Act or the regulations, the court is to take into consideration the following (so far as they are relevant)—
the impact of the offence on other persons’ rights under this Act,
the market value of any water that has been lost, misused or unlawfully taken as a consequence of the commission of the offence,
the impact, likely impact or potential impact of the offence on the spiritual, social, customary or economic use or value of land and water by or for Aboriginal people,

for an offence with an impact, likely impact or potential impact on the spiritual, social, customary or economic use or value of land and water by or for Aboriginal people—the views of Aboriginal persons impacted or likely to be impacted,
the harm, likely harm or potential harm to the environment, including, in particular, to a water source or waterfront land, by the commission of the offence,
the practical measures that may be taken to prevent, control, abate or mitigate the harm, likely harm or potential harm,
the extent to which the person could reasonably have foreseen the harm, likely harm or potential harm to the environment by the commission of the offence,
the extent to which the person had control over the causes that gave rise to the offence,
whether the offence was committed during a severe water shortage or an extreme event, including while an order is in force under section 49A, 49B or 324,
the person’s intentions in committing the offence,
whether, in committing the offence, the person was complying with orders from an employer or supervising employee,
in the case of an offence of taking water in contravention of this Act, whether the water so taken had been released for environmental purposes and, if so, whether the person was aware of that fact,
action taken under section 60G for substantially the same conduct,
a charge imposed on the person under section 91O for substantially the same conduct,
a civil penalty order made against the person for substantially the same conduct.
The court may take into consideration other matters that it considers relevant.
An authorised officer may issue a penalty notice to a person if it appears to the authorised officer that the person has committed a penalty notice offence.
A penalty notice offence is an offence against this Act or the regulations that is prescribed by the regulations as a penalty notice offence.
The Fines Act 1996 applies to a penalty notice issued under this section.

The Fines Act 1996 provides that, if a person issued with a penalty notice does not wish to have the matter determined by a court, the person may pay the amount specified in the notice and is not liable to any further proceedings for the alleged offence.

The amount payable under a penalty notice issued under this section is the amount prescribed for the alleged offence by the regulations (not exceeding the maximum amount of penalty that could be imposed for the offence by a court).
The Minister may withdraw a penalty notice within 28 days after the date on which the penalty notice is issued.
If the penalty notice is withdrawn—
the amount payable under the penalty notice ceases to be payable, and
any amount paid under the penalty notice is repayable to the person by whom it was paid, and
further proceedings in respect of the alleged offence may be taken against any person (including against the person to whom the notice was issued) as if the notice had never been issued.
This section does not limit the operation of any other provision of, or made under, this or any other Act relating to proceedings that may be taken in respect of offences.
A person is guilty of a continuing offence for each day a contravention of a legal requirement continues if—
the contravention of the legal requirement is an offence against this Act or the regulations, and
a penalty for a continuing offence is included for the offence.
A provision with a Tier 1 or 2 penalty includes a penalty for a continuing offence.
The person continues to be required to comply with the legal requirement despite a time specified for compliance having passed.
The continuing offence ceases if—
the legal requirement is complied with, or
for a legal requirement imposed by a notice—the notice is revoked or otherwise ceases to apply.
In this section—
legal requirement means a requirement imposed by the following that requires a person to do or stop doing something—
this Act,
the regulations,
a notice or direction given under this Act or the regulations,
a condition of a licence or approval.

heading.b: Legal proceedings do not affect, and are unaffected by, other action under this Act

block.txt: The prosecution of a person for an offence against this Act or the regulations, or the issue of a penalty notice in respect of such an offence, does not affect, and is unaffected by, any other action taken under this Act in relation to the act or omission giving rise to the offence.
A certificate that is issued by the Minister and that states—
that an instrument, a copy of which is set out in or annexed to the certificate, being an instrument purporting—
to be issued, made or given for the purposes of this Act, and
to have been signed by the person authorised to issue, make or give the instrument, or by another person acting as delegate or on behalf of the person,
was issued, made or given on a specified day, or
that a document, a copy of which is set out in or annexed to the certificate, is a copy of part of, or an extract from, a register or water allocation account kept under this Act, or
that an image, a copy of which is set out in or annexed to the certificate—
is a photograph or other remotely-sensed image of a specified kind, and
portrays specified land as at a specified date, or
that an amount payable under this Act by a specified person has, or has not, been paid,
is admissible in any legal proceedings and is evidence of the fact or facts so stated.
A certificate that is issued by the Minister and that states that, on a date or during a period specified in the certificate—
a specified person was, or was not, the holder of a specified access licence or approval, or
a specified access licence or approval was, at a specified time, revoked or suspended for a specified period or was revoked or suspended subject to specified conditions, or
a specified condition of an access licence or approval was, at a specified time, imposed or revoked, or
specified land was, or was not, the subject of a specified approval, or
specified land was, or was not, within a specified water management area, or
a specified part of a water source was, or was not, within a specified water management area, or
a specified water management work was, or was not, at a specified location within a specified parcel of land, or
a specified water management work was, or was not, the subject of a specified water management work approval, or
the conditions of a specified access licence or approval were, or were not, as so specified, or
the terms of a specified available water determination were, or were not, as so specified, or
a specified person was, or was not, an authorised officer in relation to a specified provision of this Act, or
a specified person was, or was not, an authorised analyst, or
a specified person was, or was not, a member of staff of the Department, or
a specified delegation under this Act was, or was not, in force, or
a specified access licence or approval was, or was not, in force, or
specified matters were, or were not, recorded in the Access Register or were, or were not, recorded in specified terms, or
the water allocations credited to, or debited or otherwise withdrawn from, the water allocation account for a specified access licence were, or were not, as so specified, or
a specified number of water allocations were, or were not, credited to, or debited or otherwise withdrawn from, the water allocation account for a specified access licence, or
a specified quantity of water was, or was not, ordered in relation to a specified access licence, or
a specified quantity of water that was taken was, or was not, taken from a specified water source or part of a specified water source, or
Part 2 or 3 of Chapter 3 of this Act does, or does not, apply to a specified water source or part of a specified water source, or
information required to be furnished to the Minister or an authorised officer pursuant to this Act was, or was not, received, or
an approved river gauge had, or had not, been maintained in accordance with the requirements (if any) prescribed by the regulations, or
the readings on an approved river gauge were, or were not, as so specified,
is admissible in any legal proceedings and is evidence of the fact or facts so stated.
In any legal proceedings, evidence is not required—
as to the accuracy or reliability of an approved river gauge, or
as to the manner in which an approved river gauge was operated,
unless evidence is adduced that the gauge was not accurate, was not reliable or was not properly operated.
For the purposes of this section, a document purporting to be a certificate under this section is, unless the contrary is proved, to be taken to be such a certificate.

In this section, approved river gauge means a gauge of a type or design approved by the Minister, by order published in the Gazette, for the purpose of measuring the level or flow of water in a river or lake.
In this section—
a reference to a water management work includes a reference to a corresponding kind of work to which Part 2, 5 or 8 of the Water Act 1912 extends, and
a reference to an approval or access licence includes a reference to an entitlement (within the meaning of clause 2 of Schedule 10) that confers a corresponding authority.
See also section 11 (1) (e) of the Natural Resources Access Regulator Act 2017 and Schedule 2 to that Act.

A certificate of an authorised analyst stating the result of an analysis or examination is admissible in evidence in any legal proceedings as evidence of the facts stated in the certificate and the correctness of the result of the analysis or examination.

A certificate of an authorised analyst that, on receipt of a container containing a sample submitted to the analyst by an authorised officer or any other person, the container was sealed and the seal securing the container was unbroken is admissible in evidence in any legal proceedings as evidence—
of the facts stated in the certificate, and
that the sample was the same sample as the one obtained by the authorised officer or other person, and
that the sample had not been tampered with before it was received by the analyst.
For the purposes of this section, a document purporting to be a certificate under this section is, unless the contrary is proved, to be taken to be such a certificate.
In proceedings for an offence or a contravention of a civil penalty provision under this Act or the regulations being taken against a landholder—
the fact that a water management work is or has been located—
on the landholder’s land, or
in a river or lake within the landholder’s land,
gives rise to a rebuttable presumption that the work was constructed by the landholder, and
the fact that a water management work is being or has been used—
on the landholder’s land, or
in a river or lake within the landholder’s land,
gives rise to a rebuttable presumption that the work is being or has been used by the landholder, and
the fact that water is being or has been taken from a water source by means of a water supply work situated—
on the landholder’s land, or
in a river or lake within the landholder’s land,
gives rise to a rebuttable presumption that the water is being or has been taken by the landholder, and

the fact that water is being or has been discharged into a water source by means of a drainage work situated on the landholder’s land gives rise to a rebuttable presumption that the water is being or has been discharged by the landholder, and
the fact that water is being or has been used on the landholder’s land gives rise to a rebuttable presumption that the water is being or has been used by the landholder, and

the fact that a controlled activity is being or has been carried out on waterfront land within the landholder’s land gives rise to a rebuttable presumption that the activity is being or has been carried out by the landholder, and

the fact that an aquifer interference activity is being or has been carried out on the landholder’s land gives rise to a rebuttable presumption that the activity is being or has been carried out by the landholder.

In proceedings for an offence or a contravention of a civil penalty provision under this Act or the regulations being taken against the holder of an approval for a water supply work, the fact that water is being or has been taken from a water source—
by means of the work, or
through metering equipment installed in connection with the work,
gives rise to a rebuttable presumption that the holder of the approval is or has been using the work to take water from that water source.
In proceedings for an offence or a contravention of a civil penalty provision under this Act or the regulations, the fact that a work of the kind referred to in—
the definition of drainage work in the Dictionary, or
paragraph (a), (b) or (c) of the definition of water supply work in the Dictionary,
is capable of being used for the purpose referred to in that provision gives rise to a rebuttable presumption that the work has been constructed or used for that purpose.
This section does not limit the operation of section 60E or 91L.
This section applies if 2 or more contraventions by a person of the same provision of this Act or the regulations arise from—
the same factual circumstances, or
the same activity being carried out at the same premises.
The contraventions may be dealt with as—
a single offence, or
a single civil penalty contravention.

heading.b: Evidence from photographs and other images

block.txt: This section applies to a photographic or other image of an area of land formed from data captured by a device carried by an aircraft, satellite or other craft, and information recorded on the image, that the Minister certifies as an approved image.
The approved image is admissible in proceedings under this Act and, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, is evidence of the following—
the matter depicted on the image,
the information recorded on the image relating to the location or boundaries of the land,
the time when, or the period during which, the image was taken,
other matters prescribed by the regulations.
In proceedings in which the approved image is admitted in evidence—
the image is presumed, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, to be orthorectified, and
evidence is not required, in the absence of evidence to the contrary, of the accuracy of a process used to—
orthorectify the image, or
determine the boundaries of land recorded in the image.

heading.b: Appeals to Land and Environment Court

block.txt: An appeal lies to the Land and Environment Court against any of the following decisions made by the Minister—
a decision refusing to grant an access licence,
a decision granting a designated access licence, if the appellant was an objector to the granting of the licence,
a decision imposing a discretionary condition on an access licence,
a decision fixing the term of an access licence,
a decision refusing consent to a dealing in an access licence,
a decision suspending or cancelling an access licence,
a decision—
in relation to the recording of any matter in the Access Register, or
in relation to the issue of any access licence certificate,
a decision refusing to grant an approval, other than a decision refusing to accept an application for an approval,
a decision granting a designated approval, if the appellant was an objector to the granting of the approval,
a decision imposing a discretionary condition on an approval,
a decision fixing the term of an approval,
a decision refusing to amend an approval in accordance with an application made by its holder,
a decision to amend an approval otherwise than on the basis of an application made by the holder of the approval,
a decision suspending or cancelling an approval or part of an approval,
a decision ordering an irrigation corporation to pay an administrative penalty to the Minister,
a decision ordering a major utility or local water utility to pay an administrative penalty to the Minister,
a decision under section 68A (1C),
a decision to require a compliance audit or audits,
a decision under section 60G,
a decision to impose a charge under section 91O,
a decision to give a direction to a person under Part 1,
a decision in relation to a bore driller’s licence, being a decision prescribed by the regulations for the purposes of this paragraph,
The following kinds of decisions may be prescribed—
decisions to refuse to grant a bore driller’s licence,
decisions to grant a bore driller’s licence subject to a condition,
decisions to vary a condition of a bore driller’s licence,
decisions to suspend or cancel a bore driller’s licence.
a decision as to a person’s entitlement to compensation for damage arising from the exercise of a power of entry under Part 2,

a decision by the Minister to give a direction to a private water corporation, private water trust or the trustees of a trust to comply with, or to cease to contravene, the rules of the corporation or trust.
An appeal lies to the Land and Environment Court against any of the following decisions—
a decision by a private water corporation or an irrigation corporation to impose a charge under section 136A or 170 on a member, landholder or other person,
a decision by a private water corporation as to a member’s water entitlement,
a decision by a private water trust or the trustees of a trust as to a member’s water entitlement.
Despite subsection (1)—
no appeal lies against any decision made by the Minister on an application to which an objection has been made if—
in the case of the applicant, the Minister has dismissed the application as a consequence of the applicant having failed to participate in mediation or neutral evaluation proceedings, or
in the case of the objector, the Minister has dismissed the objection as a consequence of the objector having failed to participate in mediation or neutral evaluation proceedings, and
no appeal lies against any decision made by the Minister pursuant to a report from a Commission of Inquiry under section 119 of the Environmental Planning and Assessment Act 1979, and
no appeal lies against a decision of the Minister to grant a licence under section 63A or 63B or to impose a discretionary condition on such a licence, and
no appeal lies against a decision of the Minister to impose a discretionary condition on a licence amended under section 68B.
An appeal is to be made in accordance with rules of court, but may not be made more than 28 days after the date on which the decision was made.
In addition to the appellant and the Minister—

the parties to an appeal made by an applicant for a designated access licence or designated approval against a decision refusing to grant the licence or approval include any objector to the granting of the licence or approval who, in accordance with rules of court, gives notice to the Land and Environment Court of the objector’s wish to become a party to the appeal, and

the parties to an appeal made by an objector to the granting of a designated access licence or designated approval against a decision granting the licence or approval include the applicant for the licence or approval.
The lodging of an appeal does not operate to stay action on the decision appealed against, except to the extent that the Land and Environment Court otherwise directs.

If the Land and Environment Court directs that a decision under appeal is stayed, the decision does not operate until the stay ceases to have effect or the Land and Environment Court confirms the decision or the appeal is withdrawn, whichever first occurs.
In this section—
designated access licence means an access licence to which a person has a right of objection under section 62.
designated approval means an approval to which a person has a right of objection under section 93.

content.txt: ch 7, pt 6, div 1: Ins 2025 No 70, Sch 3[138].

block.txt: In this part—
Court means the Land and Environment Court.

heading.b: When provision is civil penalty provision

block.txt: A provision of this Act or the regulations is a civil penalty provision if the words “Maximum civil penalty” and a civil penalty tier level are set out at the end of the provision.
The Court must not find an individual has contravened a civil penalty provision if the individual’s conduct was one or more of the following—
taking water for domestic consumption or stock watering,
installing a flood work solely to protect a dwelling,
undertaking, for the sole purpose of providing access to a dwelling, a controlled activity that does not involve impounding water,
an activity prescribed by the regulations.
This section does not apply to an individual taken to have contravened a civil penalty provision in accordance with section 370C or 370D.
In this section—
domestic consumption, in relation to land, includes domestic consumption within the meaning of section 52.
stock watering, in relation to land, includes stock watering within the meaning of section 52.

heading.b: Involvement in contravention taken to be contravention

block.txt: A person who is involved in, causes or permits a contravention of a civil penalty provision is taken to have contravened the provision.
A person is involved in a contravention of a civil penalty provision only if the person has—
aided, abetted, counselled or procured the contravention, or
induced the contravention, whether by threats or promises or otherwise, or
been knowingly involved in or a party to the contravention, whether directly or indirectly, or
conspired with others to effect the contravention.

If a corporation contravenes a civil penalty provision, each of the following persons is taken to have contravened the same provision if the person knowingly authorised or permitted the act or omission constituting the contravention—
a director of the corporation,
a person involved in the management of the corporation.
Proceedings may be taken against a person for a contravention of a civil penalty provision whether or not proceedings have been taken against the corporation.
Nothing in this section affects any liability imposed on a corporation for a contravention of a civil penalty provision by the corporation.

heading.b: Contravention by co-holders of access licence or approval

block.txt: If the holder of an access licence or approval contravenes a civil penalty provision, each co-holder of the licence or approval is taken to have contravened the same provision unless the co-holder establishes—
the contravention was committed by another person, whether or not the other person was a co-holder of the licence or approval, and
the other person was not associated with the co-holder at the time of the contravention, and
the co-holder took all reasonable steps to prevent the contravention.

Without limiting the circumstances in which a person may be associated with a co-holder, a person is associated with a co-holder for subsection (1)(b) if the person is an employee, agent, licensee, contractor or subcontractor of the co-holder.

Proceedings may be taken against the co-holder of a licence or approval for a contravention of a civil penalty provision whether or not proceedings have been taken against another person for the same contravention.
A person commits a continuing contravention for each day a contravention of a civil penalty provision of this Act or the regulations continues.
The person continues to be required to comply with a civil penalty provision despite a time specified for compliance having passed.
A continuing contravention ceases if the relevant provision is complied with.
The following table sets out the maximum civil penalties under this Act—

entry.txt: Additional penalty for each day contravention continues
Additional penalty for each day contravention continues
the greater of 45,450 penalty units or 5 times the value of the water taken
the greater of 90,900 penalty units or 5 times the value of the water taken

block.txt: In this section—
value of the water taken means the value of the water taken determined using a prescribed methodology.

content.txt: ch 7, pt 6, div 2: Ins 2025 No 70, Sch 3[138].

heading.b: Limitation period for civil penalty proceedings

block.txt: Proceedings for a contravention of a civil penalty provision may be brought within 3 years after the later of the following—
the day the contravention occurred,
the day the contravention first came to the attention of an authorised officer.

heading.b: Proceedings for contravention of civil penalty provision

block.txt: Proceedings may be brought in the Court against a person for a contravention of a civil penalty provision.
The Court must apply the rules of evidence and procedure for civil proceedings when hearing proceedings for a contravention of a civil penalty provision.

heading.b: Proceedings may be brought by Minister

block.txt: Proceedings for a contravention of a civil penalty provision may be brought by the Minister.

heading.b: Civil proceedings during or after criminal proceedings

block.txt: Proceedings against a person for a contravention of a civil penalty provision must not be commenced if criminal proceedings have been commenced against the person for an offence in relation to substantially the same conduct.

If proceedings against a person for a contravention of a civil penalty provision are underway when criminal proceedings are commenced against the person for an offence in relation to substantially the same conduct, the civil penalty provision proceedings must be dismissed by the Court.

Criminal proceedings may be commenced against a person for conduct that is substantially the same as conduct constituting a contravention of a civil penalty provision regardless of whether a civil penalty order has been made against the person.

heading.b: Evidence given in civil penalty proceedings not admissible in criminal proceedings

block.txt: Evidence of information given by an individual or evidence of the production of a document by the individual is not admissible in criminal proceedings against the individual if—

the information or document is only known to the prosecutor because the individual relied on the information or document in proceedings against the individual for a contravention of a civil penalty provision, and
the conduct alleged to constitute the offence is substantially the same as the conduct alleged to constitute the contravention of the civil penalty provision.
This section does not apply to criminal proceedings in relation to the individual giving false evidence in the proceedings for the contravention of the civil penalty provision.

heading.b: Contravention of more than one civil penalty provision

block.txt: If a person’s conduct constitutes a contravention of 2 or more civil penalty provisions, proceedings may be instituted under this Act against the person in relation to the contravention of one or more of the provisions.
Despite subsection (1), a person is not liable to more than one civil penalty under this Act for the same conduct.

heading.b: Multiple contraventions of civil penalty provision

block.txt: The Court may make a single civil penalty order against a person for multiple contraventions of a civil penalty provision if—
proceedings for the contraventions rely on the same facts, or
the contraventions form, or are part of, a series of contraventions of the same or a similar character.
The penalty must not be more than the sum of the maximum penalties that could be imposed if a separate penalty were ordered for each contravention.
The Court may direct that 2 or more proceedings for contraventions of civil penalty provisions be heard together.

heading.b: Proof of state of mind not required

block.txt: In proceedings against a person for a contravention of a civil penalty provision, it is not necessary to prove the following—
the person’s intention,
the person’s knowledge,
the person’s recklessness,
the person’s negligence,
another state of mind of the person.
Subsection (1) does not apply to proceedings for—
a contravention under section 91J(2), 340A(2) or 344(1) or (2), or
a matter that is taken, for section 370B, 370C or 370D, to be a contravention.
Despite subsection (1), the defence of honest and reasonable mistake of fact may be established.

In proceedings for a contravention of a civil penalty provision, a person who wishes to rely on an exception, exemption, excuse, qualification or justification that applies to the civil penalty provision has the evidential burden in relation to that matter.

content.txt: ch 7, pt 6, div 3: Ins 2025 No 70, Sch 3[138].

heading.b: Orders for contravention of civil penalty provision

block.txt: If the Court is satisfied a person has contravened a civil penalty provision, the Court may—
order the person to pay a monetary penalty, not more than the maximum civil penalty amount for the provision, the Court considers appropriate, and
order the person to pay an additional penalty for each day the contravention continues, and
make an order under one or more of the following as if the person had been found guilty of an offence—
section 353B,
section 353C,
section 353D,
section 353E,
section 353FB,
section 353G, and
make another order the Court considers appropriate, including an injunction.
In determining the amount to be paid by a person as a civil penalty, the Court must have regard to the following—
the nature and extent of the contravention,
the actual and potential environmental harm or detriment to the public interest resulting from the contravention,
the circumstances in which the contravention took place,
the financial or other benefit the person stood to gain from the contravention,
whether the person has previously been found, in proceedings under this Act, to have engaged in similar conduct,
whether or not action has been taken against the person under section 60G,
whether or not a charge has been imposed on the person under section 91O,
other matters the Court considers relevant.
The failure by a person to comply with an order made in accordance with subsection (1)(c) or (d) is a civil penalty contravention.
Maximum civil penalty—Tier B civil penalty.
Subsection (3) does not apply to an order made under section 353C, 353D or 353E.
The Court may, in proceedings under this part, make orders about the costs of the proceedings the Court thinks just and reasonable.
If the Court orders a person to pay a civil penalty—
the penalty is payable to the State, and
the State may enforce the order as if it were a judgment of the Court.

The Court must not make a civil penalty order against a person under this part if an order has been made against the person under a civil penalty provision of the Water Act 2007 of the Commonwealth in relation to substantially the same conduct.

heading.b: Constitution of Water Administration Ministerial Corporation

block.txt: There is constituted by this Act a corporation with the corporate name “Water Administration Ministerial Corporation”.
The affairs of the Ministerial Corporation are to be managed by the Minister.

Any act, matter or thing done in the name of, or on behalf of, the Ministerial Corporation by the Minister, or with the authority of the Minister, is taken to have been done by the Ministerial Corporation.
The Ministerial Corporation is, for the purposes of any Act, a statutory body representing the Crown.
The Ministerial Corporation has the following functions—
to construct, maintain and operate water management works,
to construct, maintain and operate gauging stations and other monitoring equipment,
to conduct research, collect information and develop technology in relation to water management,
to acquire rights to water, whether within or beyond New South Wales,
to do anything for the purpose of enabling the objects of this Act to be attained.
The Ministerial Corporation has such other functions as are conferred or imposed on it by or under this or any other Act or law.
The Ministerial Corporation may exercise its functions within and beyond New South Wales.
The Ministerial Corporation may exercise any of its functions, and may otherwise act, in the name of the Department.
It is the duty of the Ministerial Corporation to exercise its functions consistently with the principles of ecologically sustainable development.

It is the duty of the Ministerial Corporation to exercise its function of issuing a Snowy water licence under Part 5 of the Snowy Hydro Corporatisation Act 1997 consistently with the terms of the Snowy Water Inquiry Outcomes Implementation Deed.

In subsection (5), Snowy Water Inquiry Outcomes Implementation Deed means the deed under that title that was entered into on behalf of the Commonwealth, New South Wales and Victoria on 3 June 2002, as that deed is amended from time to time in accordance with its terms.
The Ministerial Corporation may install, test and remove metering equipment.
If the regulations so provide, the Ministerial Corporation has the following functions—
to maintain, repair, modify and replace metering equipment (whether or not that equipment was installed by the Corporation),
to operate metering equipment.

Regulations under subsection (2) may provide that the Ministerial Corporation is, or is not, to exercise such functions to the exclusion of any other person and may limit the exercise of the functions to—
specified water sources or classes of water sources, or
a specified area, or
specified access licences or approvals or classes of access licences or approvals in specified areas, or
specified works or classes of works.

The functions conferred by this section are in addition to any functions conferred on the Ministerial Corporation under this Act or the Water Act 1912 in relation to water management works or other works.
This section and any regulations made under this section have effect despite any other provision of this Act or the Water Act 1912.

A direction under section 326, or a condition of an access licence or approval, ceases to have effect during any period that the exercise of a function is conferred exclusively on the Ministerial Corporation by or under this section, if the direction or condition requires the exercise of, or relates to the exercise of, that function.

Subsection (6) does not affect the operation of, or enforcement of, a direction under section 326 or a condition of an access licence or approval in relation to any period before the direction or condition ceased to have effect.
In this section, a reference to an access licence or approval includes a reference to an entitlement (within the meaning of clause 2 of Schedule 10) that confers a corresponding authority.

heading.b: Interests and rights in metering equipment

block.txt: Metering equipment installed or replaced by the Ministerial Corporation is not the property of the Ministerial Corporation, except as otherwise provided by this Act or the Water Act 1912 or regulations under this Act or that Act.

No compensation is payable by or on behalf of the Crown to any person who suffers loss or damage because of the removal by the Ministerial Corporation of metering equipment installed by the Ministerial Corporation.

If a provision of the regulations provides that the Ministerial Corporation is the owner of specified metering equipment that it installs or replaces, the provision has effect despite anything contained in section 42 of the Real Property Act 1900.
With the approval of the Governor, the Ministerial Corporation may enter into commercial operations with respect to—
any services developed in connection with the exercise of its functions, and
any products or by-products (including intellectual property) resulting from the exercise of its functions, and
such other matters as may be prescribed by the regulations.
With the approval of the Governor, the Ministerial Corporation may form, or join in forming, a company, partnership or trust for the purpose of exercising its functions under this Act.

For the purposes of the Public Works Act 1912, any works carried out by the Ministerial Corporation under this Act are taken to be authorised works and the Ministerial Corporation is taken to be the Constructing Authority for those works.
Part 3 of the Public Works Act 1912 does not apply to or in respect of any works constructed by the Ministerial Corporation under this Act.
The Ministerial Corporation may acquire land for the purposes of this Act by agreement, or by compulsory process in accordance with the Land Acquisition (Just Terms Compensation) Act 1991.

The acquisition of land by the Ministerial Corporation for the purpose of its transfer to an irrigation corporation or private water corporation is taken to be for the purposes of this Act if the purpose of the transfer is to enable the irrigation corporation or private water corporation to exercise its functions under this Act.

The acquisition of land by the Ministerial Corporation for the purposes of a private water trust is taken to be for the purposes of this Act if the purpose of the acquisition is to enable the trustees of the trust or the trust to exercise functions under this Act.

For the purposes of the Public Works Act 1912, any such acquisition is taken to be for an authorised work, and the Ministerial Corporation is, in relation to that work, taken to be the Constructing Authority.
The Ministerial Corporation may arrange for the use of the services of any staff or facilities of any Public Service agency or public authority.
The Ministerial Corporation may delegate to any person the exercise of any of its functions, other than this power of delegation.
In this Part—
Board of Trustees means the Board of Trustees referred to in section 379 (4).
Fund means the Water Investment Trust Fund established by section 384.
Trust means the Water Investment Trust constituted by section 379.
There is constituted by this Act a body corporate with the corporate name of the Water Investment Trust.
The Trust has such functions as are conferred or imposed on it by or under this or any other Act or law.
The Trust is, for the purposes of any Act, a statutory body representing the Crown.
The affairs of the Trust are to be managed by a Board of Trustees.
Subject to this section, the constitution and procedure of the Board of Trustees are to be as prescribed by the regulations.
The objects of the Trust are to promote, organise, carry out and fund projects, in both the public and private sectors, for—
the restoration and rehabilitation of water sources and their dependant ecosystems, and
the construction of works for the more efficient delivery, use and recycling of water, and
the conduct of water industry adjustment, business restructuring and industry training, and
the conduct of research, and the development of technology, in relation to the matters referred to in paragraphs (a), (b) and (c),
in order to maximise the environmental, social and economic benefits of the State’s water sources for present and future generations.
The Trust may, for the purpose of promoting its objects—
make grants or loans (either conditionally or subject to conditions) for projects of the kind described in section 380, and
supervise the expenditure of money so granted, and
establish works programs, and associated budgets, for projects to be carried out or funded by the Trust, and
engage in such other activities relating to its objects as the Minister may approve.
The Trust may, with the approval of the Minister, arrange for the use of the services of any staff or facilities of a Public Service agency or public authority.
For the purposes of this Act, a person whose services are made use of under this section is an officer of the Trust.
The Trust may delegate to a member of the Board of Trustees, or to an officer of the Trust, the exercise of any of its functions, other than this power of delegation.
There is to be established in the Special Deposits Account a Water Investment Trust Fund into which are to be paid—
such money as may be raised by way of water investment contributions pursuant to this Part, and
such money as may be appropriated by Parliament for payment into the Fund, and
the proceeds of investment of money in the Fund, and
any gift or bequest of money to the Trust, and
such other money as is required or permitted to be paid into the Fund.
Money in the Trust Fund may be used—
for the purpose of enabling the Trust to exercise its functions, and
to cover the costs incurred by the Trust in administering this Part.
The Trust is to invest money in the Trust Fund—
if the Trust is a GSF agency for the purposes of Part 6 of the Government Sector Finance Act 2018—in any way that the Trust is permitted to invest money under that Part, or
if the Trust is not a GSF agency for the purposes of Part 6 of the Government Sector Finance Act 2018—in any way approved by the Treasurer.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the fixing, assessing and levying of water investment contributions from persons who hold access licences.

Water investment contributions are to be fixed in relation to specified works programs established by the Trust, and so as to yield receipts no greater in total than the amounts budgeted by the Trust in relation to the works program so specified.
For the purposes of section 78 (1) (c), a water investment contribution payable by the holder of a licence is taken to be a charge payable in respect of the licence.

Part 4 of Chapter 7 applies to and in respect of a water investment contribution levied under this section in the same way as it applies to and in respect of a rate or charge referred to in that Part and, for that purpose, the Trust is taken to be a charging authority.
In this Part—
Agreement means the Murray-Darling Basin Agreement set out in Schedule 1 to the Water Act 2007 of the Commonwealth.
Basin Officials Committee means the committee of that name established under the Agreement.
The Minister is authorised to appoint, under and in accordance with the terms of the Agreement—
a person as a member of the Basin Officials Committee representing the State, and
a person to act as the member of the Basin Officials Committee in place of the member appointed under paragraph (a).
The Minister may, at any time, terminate the appointment of any such person.
The regulations may make provision for or with respect to the appointment of, or the holding of office by, any such person.

heading.b: Minister may act for Government of NSW

block.txt: The Minister is authorised to act on behalf of the State as a Contracting Government under the Agreement.

heading.b: Authorisation of works, operations and measures under the Agreement

block.txt: Subject to the law of this State and the Agreement—
the construction, maintenance, operation and control in the State of any works under the Agreement, and
the carrying out of any of the operations referred to in the Agreement, and
the implementation of any measures referred to in the Agreement,
are authorised.

The Ministerial Corporation, Water NSW and any other public authority authorised by the Minister by notice published in the Gazette are each Constructing Authorities for the purposes of the Agreement and authorised to carry out the functions of a Constructing Authority under the Agreement.
The Minister may determine any dispute as to which authority should act as the Constructing Authority for a particular work, operation or measure.

heading.b: Certain documents to be tabled in Parliament

block.txt: The Minister is to table or cause to be tabled in each House of Parliament—
a copy of each annual report of the Murray-Darling Basin Authority received by the Minister under the Water Act 2007 of the Commonwealth, and
a copy of each amendment of the Agreement that takes effect under the terms of the Agreement,
within 15 sitting days of that House after the report is received or the amendment takes effect (as the case requires).
The Minister may appoint expert advisory panels for the purpose of this Act.
An expert advisory panel is to consist of such persons as, in the opinion of the Minister, have the qualifications and expertise appropriate to the matters proposed to be referred to it.
An expert advisory panel has the function of investigating, and reporting to the Minister on, such of the following matters as are referred to it for investigation and report—
any State Water Management Outcomes Plan to be established under section 6,
the terms of reference to be set by the Minister under section 15 for the preparation of a draft management plan,
the adequacy and appropriateness of the provisions of a draft management plan submitted to the Minister under section 37 or 40,
the effectiveness, in relation to the furthering of the water sharing principles, of any bulk access regime established by a management plan to be made by the Minister under section 41,
any management plan in respect of which a review is being carried out under section 43,
any implementation program to be established under section 51.
The Minister may establish a Water Innovation Council for the purposes of this Act.
The Water Innovation Council is to consist of such persons as, in the opinion of the Minister, have the qualifications and expertise appropriate to the function of the Council.
The function of the Water Innovation Council is to advise the Minister and Local Land Services on the identification and pursuit of measures for water conservation, including measures for—
the recovery of water (that is, preventing the loss of water from uncapped bores, porous irrigation channels, evaporation and the like), and
the re-use of water, and
the efficient use of water.
The Council is also to advise the Minister on any other matter that is referred by the Minister for advice.

Provisions with respect to the members and procedure of the Water Innovation Council or any other advisory body established under this section are, subject to any requirements of the regulations, to be determined by the Minister.
The Minister may establish advisory and other committees for the purposes of this Act.
The Minister may delegate to any person any functions conferred or imposed on the Minister by or under this Act, other than this power of delegation.

The Minister may delegate to any person any functions conferred or imposed on the Minister under any other Act, if those functions arise because of the Minister’s capacity as the Minister administering this Act or are related to that role.

Despite subsections (1) and (1A), the Secretary may sub-delegate to any person any function that has been delegated to the Secretary under this section, but only if the terms of the delegation authorise the Secretary to sub-delegate that function.

heading.b: Conferral of water management functions on public authorities

block.txt: The Minister may authorise a public authority to exercise the following functions—
assisting the Minister or a management committee in the development of, in consultations about or in the implementation of management plans,
managing licensed environmental water (within the meaning of section 8) under access licences,
monitoring water quality and other environmental health objectives of management plans (including in connection with a review or audit of any such plan).
A public authority may, with the approval of the Minister, acquire, hold and deal with access licences.
This section does not limit section 389.

heading.b: Gas and other petroleum activities—enforcement by EPA

block.txt: Schedule 2A to the Protection of the Environment Operations Act 1997 (Enforcement of gas and other petroleum legislation) applies to this Act, and the operation of this Act is subject to that Schedule.
The Minister may appoint authorised officers, either for the purposes of this Act generally or for the purposes of any specified provisions of this Act.
The Minister may appoint authorised analysts for the purposes of this Act.
See also section 11 (1) (e) of the Natural Resources Access Regulator Act 2017 and Schedule 2 to that Act.

heading.b: Resolution of disputes between public authorities

block.txt: Any dispute arising between two or more public authorities as to the exercise of their functions under this Act is to be resolved—
by agreement between the Ministers responsible for them, or
if the dispute is between Ministers, by the Premier.
Each public authority must comply with any directions arising out of the resolution of the dispute under this section.

heading.b: Interstate arrangements in relation to access licences and approvals

block.txt: The Minister may enter into arrangements with a Minister of any other State or Territory with respect to the carrying out of administrative functions in relation to access licences or approvals, and their equivalents in the other State or Territory, pursuant to section 71W or 89.
Without limiting subsection (1), such arrangements may be made with respect to the following—
the collection of fees, charges and administrative penalties,
the keeping of water allocation accounts.
For the purposes of this Act, the rights to the control, use and flow of—
all water in rivers, lakes and aquifers, and
all water conserved by any works that are under the control or management of the Minister, and
all water occurring on or below the surface of the ground (including overland flow water flowing over or lying there for the time being) other than water referred to in subsection (1A),
are the State’s water rights.
Subsection (1) (c) does not include any of the following—
water that is collected from a roof (including water collected from a roof using a rainwater tank),
water occurring on or below the surface of the ground in such other circumstances as may be prescribed by the regulations.
The State’s water rights are vested in the Crown, except to the extent to which they are divested from the Crown by or under this or any other Act.
The State’s water rights prevail over any authority conferred by or under any other Act or law, except to the extent to which this or any other Act expressly so provides.
The State’s water rights are not to be exercised in contravention of—
the powers conferred by section 15 of the Fire and Rescue NSW Act 1989 and section 26 of the Rural Fires Act 1997 on an officer in charge at a fire or hazardous material incident, or
the rights and obligations of the Snowy Hydro Company under a Snowy water licence within the meaning of the Snowy Hydro Corporatisation Act 1997, or
the rights conferred by the Local Land Services Act 2013 with respect to the watering of stock at stock watering places within the meaning of that Act.

heading.b: Abolition of common law riparian rights

block.txt: Any right that the owner of riparian land would, but for this section, have at common law with respect to the flow of any river, estuary or lake through or past the land, or to the taking or using of water from any such river, estuary or lake, is hereby abolished.
A document authorised or required by this Act or the regulations to be served on a person may be served by the following methods—
for an individual—by personal delivery to the person,
by post to the address specified by the person for the service of documents of that kind,
for an individual who has not specified an address—by post to the residential or business address of the person last known to the person serving the document,
for a corporation—by post to the registered office or another office of the corporation or by leaving the document at the office with a person who is apparently more than 16 years of age,
if the person has consented, whether explicitly or impliedly, to service of documents generally or documents of that kind by electronic communication—by electronic communication,

heading.b: Examples of impliedly consenting to service of documents by electronic communication—

block.txt: previously using email to correspond with the person or authority serving the document or including an email address in an application to, or other official communication with, the person or authority
by another method authorised by the regulations for the service of documents of that kind.

In the case of land that is owned or occupied by more than one person or of an approval that is held by more than one person, service of a document on any one of them, or on any person duly appointed by them for the purpose of accepting service of documents, is taken to be service on all of them.
This section does not limit any other manner in which a document may be served.
In this section—
electronic communication has the same meaning as in the Electronic Transactions Act 2000.
serve includes give or send.

heading.b: Methodologies for determining water volume and value

block.txt: The regulations may prescribe methodologies by which a determination of the following may be made for the purposes of this Act—
a volume of water,
the value of water.
A prescribed methodology may be used to determine a volume of water if—
a provision of this Act or the regulations expressly provides for the use of a prescribed methodology, or
an actual measurement is unavailable, including due to the absence of metering equipment or a fault in metering equipment.
A prescribed methodology must be used to determine the value of water if a provision of this Act or the regulations expressly provides for the use of a prescribed methodology.
A methodology may be prescribed for—
one or more specific provisions of this Act or the regulations, or
all provisions of this Act and the regulations.

heading.b: Publication of notices, orders and proclamations in authorised manner

block.txt: A requirement of this Act that a notice be published in the authorised manner is a requirement that the notice be published in a manner that the Minister is satisfied is likely to bring the notice to the attention of members of the public in the area that is affected by the notice or its subject matter.
In this section, notice includes an order or proclamation.
The Minister must ensure a consolidated register of information recorded in registers under this Act is kept and made publicly available in accordance with this section (the public water register).
The public water register must contain the following—
information recorded in the following registers that is, in the Minister’s opinion, appropriate for inclusion in the public water register—
the Access Register,
the register of available water determinations referred to in section 84,
the register of approvals referred to in section 113,
other information that is, in the Minister’s opinion, appropriate for inclusion in the public water register,
information given to the Minister under section 87E,
other information prescribed by the regulations.
The public water register must not contain the following—
personal information within the meaning of the Privacy and Personal Information Protection Act 1998, Part 6,
other information prescribed by the regulations.
The public water register must be published on a publicly accessible website with an electronic search facility.
The regulations may make further provision about the public water register.

heading.b: Continuing effect of directions and conditions

block.txt: A direction given, or a condition of a licence or approval imposed, under this Act or the regulations that specifies a time by which, or period within which, the direction or condition must be complied with continues to have effect until the direction or condition is complied with even though the time has passed or the period has expired.
A direction that does not specify a time by which, or period within which, the direction must be complied with continues to have effect until the direction is complied with.
This section does not apply to the extent that any requirement under a direction or a condition of a licence or approval is revoked.
Nothing in this section affects the powers of the Minister with respect to the enforcement of a direction or a condition of a licence or approval.
This Act binds the Crown in right of New South Wales and, in so far as the legislative power of Parliament permits, the Crown in all its capacities.
An act or omission of—
the Minister or the Secretary, or
a prescribed authority, or a member or trustee of a prescribed authority, or
a member of staff of the Department or of a prescribed authority, or
an authorised person appointed under Chapter 7, Part 1, Division 9, or
a person acting under the direction of a person referred to in paragraph (a), (b), (c) or (c1),

does not subject the Minister, Secretary, member of staff or person so acting personally to any action, liability, claim or demand if the act or omission was done, or omitted to be done, in good faith for the purpose of executing this Act.
In this section, prescribed authority means—
the Ministerial Corporation, or
the Regulator, or
the Water Investment Trust, or the Board of Trustees of the Water Investment Trust, or
a management committee, or
a water supply authority, or
a private water corporation, or
the administrator of a private water corporation or a private water trust, or
a private water trust, or
an irrigation corporation.
Neither the Crown nor any other person is subject to any action, liability, claim or demand arising—
from the unavailability of water, or
from any failure in the quantity or quality of water, or
from the release of water for environmental purposes,

as a consequence of anything done or omitted to be done in good faith by the Minister, by a prescribed authority or by any person acting on behalf of the Minister or a prescribed authority, in the exercise of any functions under this Act or the Water NSW Act 2014.
Neither the Crown nor any other person is subject to any action, liability, claim or demand arising as a consequence of—
the use in good faith of any water management work, or
the release in good faith of water from any water management work,
by the Minister, by a prescribed authority or by any person acting on behalf of the Minister or a prescribed authority, in the exercise of any functions under this Act or the Water NSW Act 2014.
In this section, prescribed authority means—
the Ministerial Corporation, or
a water supply authority, or
Water NSW.

The annual reporting information prepared for the Department under the Government Sector Finance Act 2018 is to include a report on the Minister’s work and activities under this Act for the annual reporting period to which that information relates, and may also include the annual reporting information prepared for the Ministerial Corporation.

The regulations may make provision for or with respect to a scheme to facilitate consultation and negotiations with owners and occupiers of land, and other persons, who may be affected by proposed releases of water for environmental purposes.
Without limiting subsection (1), the regulations may make provision for or with respect to the following—
the circumstances in which the scheme will apply,
notification of proposed releases,
mediation of disputes, in cases where agreement is required to resolve legal or other issues relating to a proposed release.
The Governor may make regulations about a matter that is—
required or permitted by this Act to be prescribed, or
necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
In particular, the regulations may make provision about—
the forms to be used in connection with the administration of this Act, and
the fees and charges to be imposed in connection with the administration of this Act, and the circumstances under which fees and charges may be waived, reduced and remitted, and
the requirement for security deposits and the amount of security, including the circumstances in which the Minister may determine the amount, and
the circumstances in which security deposits are forfeited and the application of money arising from the forfeiture of security deposits, and
the regulation and control of bore drilling and the licensing of bore drillers, and
the information to be provided to the Minister by the holder of any approval under this Act, including the circumstances in which any such information must be verified by statutory declaration, and
the regulation of vessels and works on or along the Murray River, including the following—
the regulation and control of vessels at or near locks, weirs and other works,
the management and control of works.

A regulation may make provision for or with respect to the exemption of any person, matter or thing from the operation of this Act or any specified provision of this Act, either unconditionally or subject to conditions.
A regulation may create an offence punishable by a penalty not exceeding—
for a corporation—200 penalty units, or
otherwise—100 penalty units.
A regulation may apply, adopt or incorporate any publication as in force from time to time.

The regulations may declare a matter that is dealt with by this Act or the regulations to be an excluded matter for the purposes of section 250C of the Water Act 2007 of the Commonwealth in relation to—
the whole of the Commonwealth water legislation, or
a specified provision of that legislation, or
that legislation other than a specified provision, or
that legislation otherwise than to a specified extent.

Section 250C of the Water Act 2007 of the Commonwealth provides that if a State law declares a matter to be an excluded matter for the purposes of that section in relation to all or part of the Commonwealth water legislation, then the provisions that are the subject of the declaration will not apply in relation to that matter in the State concerned.
In this section—
Commonwealth water legislation has the same meaning as it has in the Water Act 2007 of the Commonwealth.
matter includes act, omission, body, person or thing.

The regulations may declare any provision of this Act to be a Commonwealth water legislation displacement provision for the purposes of section 250D of the Water Act 2007 of the Commonwealth (either generally or specifically in relation to a provision of that Commonwealth Act).

Section 250D of the Water Act 2007 of the Commonwealth enables a State to displace the operation of provisions of that Act that are declared under a State law to be Commonwealth water legislation displacement provisions for the purposes of that section.
The Acts listed in Schedule 7 are repealed.
Each Act listed in Schedule 8 is amended as set out in that Schedule.

heading.b: Uncommenced amendments to Act transferred to Act

block.txt: The provisions of Schedule 13A are transferred provisions to which the Interpretation Act 1987, section 30A applies.
Schedules 9, 10 and 11 have effect.
The Minister is to review this Act to determine whether the policy objectives of the Act remain valid and whether the terms of the Act remain appropriate for securing those objectives.
The review is to be undertaken as soon as possible after the period of 5 years from the date of assent to this Act.
A report on the outcome of the review is to be tabled in each House of Parliament within 12 months after the end of the period of 5 years.
(Section 71C)

heading.b: Registration of access licences, security interests and caveats over access licences and other matters

block.txt: The Minister registers an access licence granted by the Minister under section 63, 63A or 63B by recording in the Access Register in such form as the Minister considers appropriate the following—
the name of each holder or co-holder of the access licence,
details of entitlements conferred on the holder or co-holders by the licence,
if the licence is co-held, details of the arrangements under which the licence is held by the co-holders (the co-holder’s tenancy arrangement),
any water supply work, or group of water supply works, nominated as a work or group of works by means of which water allocations under the licence may be taken,
any adaptive environmental water condition to which the licence, or a part of the licence, is subject.

The Minister registers any Ministerial action (other than the grant of an access licence under section 63, 63A or 63B) by recording in the Access Register the details of the action in such form as the Minister considers appropriate.
The Minister must not register an access licence or any Ministerial action until—
if an appeal is made against the decision within that time, at or after the time the appeal is finally disposed of.

The Minister may include in the Access Register such other information about the holder of an access licence and the conditions of, and other matters relating to, the licence as the Minister considers appropriate.

heading.b: Registration of dealings in access licences and holdings in access licences

block.txt: A party to a dealing in an access licence or holding in an access licence may make an application to the Minister in the approved form for the dealing to be registered in the Access Register.
The application must be accompanied—
by an instrument evidencing the dealing, and
by such other documents (if any) as the Minister may require, and
by such fee (if any) as approved by the Minister.

This clause has a similar effect in relation to registration of dealings in access licences and holdings in access licences to the effect section 41 of the Real Property Act 1900 has in relation to registration of dealings in estates or interests in land.
The Minister must (unless anything recorded in the Access Register prevents the registration of the dealing)—
register the dealing by recording in the Access Register the particulars of the names of the parties to the dealing, a description of the dealing and the time and date of the recording.
